title: End-to-End Differentiable Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics for Fluid--Rigid Optimization with Gradient Stabilization

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an end-to-end differentiable Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) optimization framework for fluid-rigid body coupling with a gradient stabilization mechanism. It enables reliable reverse-mode differentiation through long rollouts for challenging control and inverse-design tasks.
AI.motivation: Propagating useful sensitivities through long SPH rollouts is difficult because rapidly changing particle neighborhoods, contacts, and pressure responses make reverse-mode gradients noisy and cause adjoint variables to explode.
AI.method: The authors formulate an SPH-specific reverse-mode pipeline for IISPH-based fluid-rigid simulation with vector-Jacobian products in checkpointed segments, paired with a self-adaptive adjoint correction sequence that acts as a descent-preserving preconditioner to bound adjoint amplification while preserving update direction alignment.
AI.result: Experiments across impulse and shape optimization, scalar-amplitude water actuation, multi-object water-jet balancing, and neural fluid-mediated pendulum control show that stabilized reverse-mode differentiation supports complex optimization tasks.
AI.conclusion: Stabilizing reverse-mode gradients makes long-horizon SPH-based fluid-rigid optimization practical for inverse design and high-dimensional control.

title: Refit Always —Precomputed Ensembles of Bounding Volume Hierarchies for Parametric Animations

AI.tldr: This paper presents a parametric Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) method that precomputes a small ensemble of BVH topologies for parametric animations and refits the selected topology at runtime. It achieves high-quality BVHs at refit-level runtime costs, outperforming per-frame LBVH rebuilds.
AI.motivation: Rebuilding a BVH every frame for animated geometry is often too expensive for real-time budgets, while existing amortization strategies such as refitting or infrequent rebuilds degrade BVH quality.
AI.method: The method precomputes a small set of BVH topologies that jointly cover the animation's pose space with low error, then selects the appropriate topology for the current pose at runtime and performs a refit.
AI.result: Evaluated on skeletal animations from the Mixamo dataset, the approach matches high-quality BVH builders and achieves 1.25x lower SAH costs with 2.4x lower runtimes compared to per-frame LBVH rebuilding.
AI.conclusion: Precomputed BVH ensembles with runtime refitting offer a practical way to maintain high traversal quality for parametric animations within tight real-time frame budgets.

title: Recovering Projective Dynamics: Strain‐Based ADMM for Cosserat Rod Simulation

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a strain-based Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) formulation for Cosserat rod simulation that recovers the fast local-global architecture of Projective Dynamics (PD). It converges faster and exhibits less numerical damping than prior ADMM variants under realistic high stiffness ratios.
AI.motivation: Classic PD converges poorly under extreme stretch-shear to bend-twist stiffness ratios in realistic Cosserat rods, while existing ADMM extensions incur nonlinear local solve overhead and noticeable damping under tight iteration budgets.
AI.method: The framework defines auxiliary variables at the strain level and applies a two-level relaxation via Block Coordinate Descent and PD to avoid nonlinear local solves, alongside an augmented orientation block for bending-twisting constraints and a penalty parameter clamping strategy.
AI.result: Experiments on trees and hair under physically realistic parameters show faster convergence than previous ADMM variants, a 21% total runtime reduction in a representative high stiffness ratio scenario, and reduced numerical damping without per-scene penalty tuning.
AI.conclusion: Strain-based ADMM bridges the efficiency of Projective Dynamics and the robustness of ADMM for simulating stiff slender structures.

title: Projective Affine Body Dynamics for Multibody Systems

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a GPU-friendly variational algorithm within affine body dynamics for simulating constrained multibody systems with nonlinear constraints, contact, and friction. It enables real-time simulation of rigid and flexible body interactions without assembling a global Hessian.
AI.motivation: Simulating multibody systems is challenging due to non-smooth contact handling, nonlinearity in flexible joints, and parallelization bottlenecks.
AI.method: The authors reformulate constrained multibody dynamics into a variational form modeling affine bodies connected by peridynamic bonds, and solve the resulting nonlinear optimization in a global-local iterative manner using semi-implicit successive substitution.
AI.result: By avoiding global Hessian assembly, the algorithm maps efficiently to GPUs and achieves real-time simulation of intricate rigid and flexible body interactions involving contact, joint constraints, and friction.
AI.conclusion: Unifying affine body dynamics, constraints, and contact via peridynamic bonds provides a scalable, parallelizable foundation for real-time multibody simulation.

title: PCAD‐Flow: Point Clouds Anomaly Detection via Normalizing Flow

AI.tldr: This paper proposes PCAD-Flow, a conditional normalizing flow framework for unsupervised 3D point cloud anomaly detection and localization via exact likelihood estimation. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on Real3D-AD and Anomaly-ShapeNet.
AI.motivation: Existing unsupervised 3D point cloud anomaly detection methods rely indirectly on feature matching, reconstruction errors, or geometric deviations rather than directly modeling point-wise feature densities.
AI.method: PCAD-Flow uses conditional normalizing flows to map point-wise features to a tractable latent distribution for direct negative log-likelihood anomaly scoring, supported by a Progressive Local Conditioning (PLC) module that aggregates multi-stage neighborhood context.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on Real3D-AD and Anomaly-ShapeNet show that PCAD-Flow achieves state-of-the-art object-level anomaly detection and point-level localization, with substantial localization gains on real-world benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Context-aware density modeling with normalizing flows provides a direct and accurate alternative to indirect deviation measures for 3D point cloud anomaly detection.

title: Wide SOBB Hierarchies for Ray Tracing of Dynamic Scenes

AI.tldr: This paper presents algorithms for constructing compressed wide Bounding Volume Hierarchies (BVHs) with Skewed Oriented Bounding Boxes (SOBBs) and refitting them for dynamic scenes. The approach speeds up secondary ray traversal over wide AABB BVHs while making SOBB refitting over 3x faster than prior SOBB refit methods.
AI.motivation: While SOBBs offer tighter bounds than AABBs, existing SOBB hierarchies lack efficient compressed wide BVH construction and fast refitting algorithms with low scratch memory for dynamic scenes.
AI.method: The authors develop construction algorithms for compressed wide SOBB BVHs and a new refit algorithm that reduces both computation and scratch memory requirements.
AI.result: The method yields 1.07x to 1.6x faster secondary ray traversal than compressed wide AABB BVHs (up to 10x in extreme cases) at the cost of 1.15x slower builds and 7 to 15 extra bits per node, while the new refit is over 3x faster with roughly 4x less scratch memory (about 1.45x slower than wide AABB refit).
AI.conclusion: Efficient construction and lightweight refitting make compressed wide SOBB hierarchies a viable option for real-time ray tracing of dynamic scenes.

title: Neural Toroidal Patch: On Smooth Meshes, the Presence of a Local Analytic Base Matters More Than Its Form or the Network Architecture

AI.tldr: Using the Neural Toroidal Patch (NTP) representation on smooth meshes, this study shows that having a local analytic geometric base matters far more for surface accuracy than the base's specific form or the neural network architecture.
AI.motivation: In neural surface representation, it is unclear how much the presence of a geometric prior contributes relative to its specific mathematical form or the complexity of the network architecture.
AI.method: NTP decomposes a triangle mesh into osculating torus patches via curvature-based fitting and trains an MLP to predict a small scalar residual along the torus normal, which the authors systematically ablate against different analytic bases (paraboloid, tangent plane), network architectures, and base-free baselines.
AI.result: A flat 3-layer MLP with 41K parameters matches or slightly outperforms a 3.7x larger hierarchical design, and torus, paraboloid, and tangent-plane bases perform within 1.2x at vertices (2x continuously), whereas removing the analytic base degrades accuracy by an order of magnitude; the learned residual also transfers to held-out meshes, halving error when tuning only per-patch latent codes.
AI.conclusion: For smooth meshes, incorporating an analytic local base acts as a strong data-efficient regularizer and is more critical than network architecture or the exact choice of local approximant.

title: STITCH: Structure Tensor Informed Topologically Coherent Hair Reconstruction

AI.tldr: This paper introduces STITCH, a sparse hierarchical multi-view hair reconstruction framework based on an ambiguous structure tensor representation. It significantly improves strand-level fidelity and structural coherence on curly, heavily occluded hairstyles.
AI.motivation: Learned hair reconstruction priors struggle to generalize across diverse hairstyles, while implicit orientation fields collapse multi-modal strand orientations into locally averaged estimates in occluded regions.
AI.method: STITCH encodes local orientation distributions using an ambiguous structure tensor to defer directional commitment until global evidence is aggregated, combines boundary-driven helical continuation to propagate surface structure into occluded interiors, and uses consensus-based disambiguation with cross-view orientation regularization.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate substantial improvements in strand-level fidelity and structural coherence on highly occluded, curly, and geometrically complex hairstyles.
AI.conclusion: Preserving directional ambiguity during multi-view aggregation and resolving it via global consensus enables accurate, topologically coherent 3D hair reconstruction without relying on restrictive learned priors.

title: Beyond Horizontal Refinement: Extending Quadtree Tall Cells with Adaptive Optical Layers

AI.tldr: This paper presents Extended Quadtree Tall Cells, an adaptive grid framework for large-scale liquid simulation that adds optical-layer thickness as a degree of freedom. It reduces computational cost compared to Quadtree Tall Cells while maintaining comparable visual quality.
AI.motivation: Quadtree Tall Cells lose efficiency when large portions of a liquid surface exhibit fine-scale details or high-frequency oscillations, as this triggers extensive horizontal quadtree subdivision.
AI.method: The framework introduces adaptive optical-layer thickness alongside adaptive horizontal resolution on top of Quadtree Tall Cells to reduce pressure degrees of freedom even in highly refined surface regions.
AI.result: Experimental results show that the proposed method lowers computational cost relative to Quadtree Tall Cells while preserving comparable visual quality, especially in scenes with complex free-surface motion.
AI.conclusion: Jointly adapting horizontal resolution and optical-layer thickness extends the scalability of tall-cell grids for detailed large-scale liquid simulations.

title: PASTEL: Palette‐Affinity Soft Color Segmentation with Texture‐Preserving Editing Layers

AI.tldr: This paper proposes PASTEL, a palette-conditioned soft color segmentation framework for localized recoloring that decomposes images into palette-associated alpha layers and residual-enhanced color layers. It balances reconstruction fidelity, editability, and inference efficiency.
AI.motivation: Existing soft color segmentation methods for texture-rich recoloring struggle to simultaneously achieve high reconstruction fidelity, clean alpha-layer editability, and fast inference, often losing high-frequency details or ignoring explicit pixel-palette relationships.
AI.method: PASTEL encodes image pixels and palette colors into a shared feature space to compute normalized pixel-palette affinity alpha layers, and uses a lightweight predictor for palette-constrained residual refinement trained with reconstruction, sparsity, and residual-distance objectives.
AI.result: Experiments demonstrate that PASTEL achieves a favorable balance among reconstruction fidelity, localized editability, alpha-layer compactness, and inference efficiency, and also supports palette retrieval.
AI.conclusion: Combining pixel-palette affinity learning with palette-constrained residual refinement enables fast, high-fidelity, and editable localized recoloring for design workflows.

title: HLoD: Screen‐Space Hierarchical Level‐of‐Detail Traversal for 3D Gaussian Splatting

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Hierarchical Level of Detail (HLoD) for 3D Gaussian Splatting, which jointly optimizes Gaussian levels into a single explicit parent-child hierarchy with dynamic GPU traversal. It enables smooth perceptual LoD transitions and continuous performance-quality scaling.
AI.motivation: Standard 3DGS lacks an inherent hierarchy so rasterization scales with fine scene details rather than visible features, while existing LoD methods train discrete levels independently and suffer from abrupt transitions.
AI.method: HLoD jointly optimizes a single parent-child tree using hierarchy-aware pruning, parent-child regularization, and scale safeguards, and integrates an efficient GPU traversal that collapses sibling groups based on local pixel-projection thresholds directly into optimization.
AI.result: Evaluations show competitive reconstruction quality with minimal traversal overhead, enabling continuous control over performance-quality trade-offs via pixel-projection thresholds and selective hierarchical memory scaling, while demonstrating that joint optimization is essential over post-hoc hierarchies.
AI.conclusion: Jointly optimizing an explicit parent-child hierarchy with integrated screen-space traversal provides smooth, adaptive Level-of-Detail rendering for 3D Gaussian Splatting.

title: Construction of Simple Quadrangulations of the Sphere at Skeletal Joints

AI.tldr: This paper presents a method for constructing crossing-free simple quadrangulations of the sphere from unordered direction vectors for parametric volumetric modeling of skeletal joints. The resulting primal graphs convert directly into exact rational Bezier shell and column volumes.
AI.motivation: Parametric volumetric modeling of skeletal joints and multi-joint truss lattices requires valid, crossing-free spherical quadrangulations derived from arbitrary sets of outgoing branch directions.
AI.method: The method enumerates candidate dual graphs to select a topology prioritizing quad convexity and regularity, realizes it on the sphere without crossings via a conflict-constrained assignment problem with lazy cyclic-order separation, and converts the primal graph into exact rational Bezier volumes.
AI.result: Experiments on spherical Fibonacci sampling direction sets of size 3 to 20 show that the method robustly produces valid, high-quality quadrangulations across diverse configurations and extends naturally to multi-joint 3D lattice assemblies.
AI.conclusion: Automated crossing-free spherical quadrangulation enables compact, exact rational Bezier volumetric representations for skeletal joints and complex 3D truss structures.

title: Text‐Inspired Feature Refinement for Few‐Shot 3D Point Cloud Semantic Segmentation

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a few-shot 3D point cloud semantic segmentation framework that refines 3D features using geometric dependencies and text-derived semantic anchors. It outperforms state-of-the-art methods by 5.69% and 9.66% mIoU on S3DIS and ScanNet.
AI.motivation: Recent few-shot 3D point cloud semantic segmentation methods focus heavily on prototype enhancement while neglecting the quality of the underlying 3D feature representations.
AI.method: The framework introduces a Channel-Aware Feature Purification (CAFP) module to mine intra-channel correlations, a Text-Anchored Modality Adaptation (TAMA) module using class text embeddings to align features and reduce the support-query gap, and a Text-Geometry (TG) loss to transfer inter-class semantic relationships.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that the method outperforms prior state-of-the-art approaches by 5.69% mIoU on S3DIS and 9.66% mIoU on ScanNet.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly refining 3D features through channel-wise geometric purification and text-anchored semantic alignment substantially improves few-shot 3D point cloud segmentation.

title: Memory‐Guided Multi‐Constraint Deep Unrolling for Robust Phase Unwrapping

AI.tldr: This paper proposes MM-DPU, a memory-guided multi-constraint deep unfolding framework for robust phase unwrapping across diverse imaging modalities. It improves physical consistency and structural accuracy under noise and wrapping ambiguities.
AI.motivation: Phase unwrapping remains difficult in the presence of noise, discontinuities, and severe wrapping ambiguities across graphics, depth sensing, holography, and remote sensing.
AI.method: MM-DPU unfolds iterative optimization into stages alternating between wrapped-gradient data consistency and a dual-branch phase-prior network, connected by a dual residual memory mechanism and trained with a hybrid unsupervised wrapped-gradient and supervised phase-gradient loss.
AI.result: Experiments on time-of-flight imaging, compressive holographic video, and Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar demonstrate strong robustness and generalization across diverse phase unwrapping scenarios.
AI.conclusion: Combining dual residual memory with multi-constraint deep unrolling provides a generalizable and physically consistent solution for challenging phase unwrapping tasks.

title: Real‐Time Bijective Planar Maps

AI.tldr: This paper describes a simple real-time algorithm for computing bijective planar maps between two simply-connected bounded domains from boundary point correspondences using a composition of two harmonic maps.
AI.motivation: Interactive shape deformation systems require fast, guaranteed bijective mappings between planar domains constrained by user-specified boundary correspondences.
AI.method: The algorithm maps both domains to the unit disk via conformal maps, computes a harmonic map between the two disks matching the boundary constraints, and composes them into a double harmonic map extended piecewise linearly with harmonic coordinates over triangulations.
AI.result: For three correspondences the map reduces to a classical conformal Mobius transformation, and in general it provides a smooth tradeoff between conformality and harmonicity at interactive speeds.
AI.conclusion: Double harmonic maps offer a simple, efficient, and guaranteed bijective parameterization tool for real-time 2D shape deformation.

title: Physically Based Rendering in the Latent Space

AI.tldr: This paper introduces physically based rendering directly in the latent feature space of variational autoencoders used by generative image diffusion models. Trained on a single rendered image, it enables physically guided content generation under changing geometry, lighting, and camera views.
AI.motivation: Image diffusion models offer high visual quality but lack the fine-grained physical controllability of classical computer graphics rendering pipelines.
AI.method: The authors modify the rendering equation to simulate light transport in the pretrained VAE latent space and pair it with a differentiable renderer to optimize scene parameters with minimal refinement.
AI.result: Trained on a single rendered image, the method generalizes to changes in scene geometry, lighting conditions, and camera viewpoints.
AI.conclusion: Bridging light transport simulation with generative latent spaces opens a path toward controllable, physically grounded neural rendering.

title: WPDv2: Implicit‐Assisted Poisson‐Disk Resampling with Sharp Feature Preservation

AI.tldr: This paper proposes WPDv2, a training-free, implicit-assisted Poisson-disk resampling framework for point clouds that preserves sharp features under noise and incompleteness.
AI.motivation: Existing point cloud resampling methods struggle to simultaneously maintain global coverage, spatial regularity, and sharp feature preservation when inputs are noisy, incomplete, or non-uniform.
AI.method: WPDv2 integrates implicit surface reconstruction to establish a coherent geometric domain, uses a winding number-guided sharpness field for density-adaptive sampling, and applies feature-constrained Voronoi relaxation for spatial regularity.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that WPDv2 achieves superior sharp feature preservation and robust resampling performance on noisy and incomplete point clouds.
AI.conclusion: Coupling implicit surface reconstruction with winding-number sharpness weighting provides a practical, training-free solution for high-fidelity point cloud resampling.

title: Prompt‐Conditioned Cue Matching for Black‐Box Procedural Material Fitting

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Prompt-Conditioned Cue Matching, a target-relative CLIP response loss that uses text prompts to emphasize specific visual cues during black-box procedural material fitting.
AI.motivation: In black-box parameter fitting for non-differentiable procedural shaders, global CLIP image matching often underweights residual visual cues such as color, feature scale, stripe spacing, gloss, or cellular structure.
AI.method: The method pairs standard CLIP image matching in an image-dominant hybrid loss with a target-relative CLIP response term where a text prompt specifies which visual cue to compare more closely between the target and candidate renders.
AI.result: Experiments on checker, noise, wave, and Voronoi shaders, along with a real-capture verification, demonstrate that language-defined cue responses enable targeted refinement of remaining visual discrepancies.
AI.conclusion: Prompt-conditioned cue matching provides an effective way to steer black-box procedural material optimization toward subtle, user-specified appearance attributes.

title: Blended Chart Surfaces: A Seamless Explicit Representation for Smooth Surface Fitting

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Blended Chart Surfaces (BCS), a compact, network-free explicit surface representation that guarantees global smoothness and supports arbitrary topologies. It achieves a favorable trade-off between simplicity, expressivity, and access to differential quantities.
AI.motivation: Existing neural surface representations either require iso-surfacing (implicit fields) or suffer from canonical-domain parameterization constraints and seam artifacts between local charts (explicit neural maps).
AI.method: Given a coarse proxy mesh encoding topology, BCS jointly optimizes a polynomial map at each proxy vertex via an off-the-shelf optimizer and fuses neighboring maps using a smooth one-ring coordinate blending scheme that is equivariant to rigid motions and scaling.
AI.result: Evaluations across diverse topologies and geometric complexities against interpolating-function baselines and mesh-displacement MLPs show that BCS delivers strong expressivity, compactness, and direct, stable access to derivatives and surface energies without patch-boundary seams.
AI.conclusion: Blending local polynomial charts over a coarse proxy mesh provides a simple, globally smooth, and differentiable explicit representation for geometry processing.

title: Angle‐Based Metric Adaptation for Quadrangulation

AI.tldr: This paper presents an angle-based metric optimization method for feature-aware quadrangulation that uses triangle angles as primary variables. It improves frame-field integrability and parameterization robustness on CAD models.
AI.motivation: Existing metric optimization methods for quadrangulation optimize symmetric positive definite tensors directly, making integrability, feature, and injectivity constraints nonlinear and harder to solve robustly.
AI.method: By parameterizing the metric with triangle angles, local flatness, sharp features, and corners become linear constraints, positive frame orientation reduces to simple box constraints, and sizing, conformality, isometric regularization, and singularity controls are formulated as mostly convex terms.
AI.result: Experiments on CAD models demonstrate improved frame-field integrability and higher parameterization robustness compared to existing tensor-based approaches.
AI.conclusion: Formulating metric adaptation in terms of triangle angles yields a mostly convex, robust, and flexible optimization framework for feature-aware quadrangulation.

title: CamLoop4D: Controllable 4D Scene Generation by Closing the Camera Loop between Generation and Reconstruction

AI.tldr: This paper presents CamLoop4D, a controllable 4D scene generation framework that couples a camera-conditioned video diffusion model and a 4D Gaussian reconstructor via a shared Plucker trajectory tensor. It eliminates pose re-estimation and achieves state-of-the-art PSNR/SSIM and user preference on 4D benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Cascading video generators with 4D reconstructors via pose estimation compounds estimation errors with generation artifacts, degrading geometric and temporal consistency.
AI.method: CamLoop4D closes the loop by having both the video diffusion model and the 4D Gaussian reconstructor operate directly on the same Plucker trajectory tensor, and introduces hybrid motion bases combining six fixed se(3) rigid generators with learnable non-rigid bases to reduce motion-bank storage from O(B*F) to O(B).
AI.result: CamLoop4D achieves the best PSNR/SSIM on the iPhone benchmark, the highest user preference against seven baselines in text-to-4D and image-to-4D tasks, and generates an 80-frame 960x720 scene in roughly 40 minutes on a single RTX 3090 with 20 fps playback.
AI.conclusion: Closing the camera loop with a shared Plucker representation and compact hybrid motion bases makes high-fidelity, controllable 4D content creation accessible on consumer GPUs.

title: Function‐Aware Regional Injection for Training‐Free Image Editing

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Function-Aware Regional Injection (FARI), a training-free image editing framework for MMDiT-based flow models that tailors source feature injection to the functional roles of transformer blocks.
AI.motivation: Training-free editing via source feature injection struggles to balance content preservation and modification across diverse edit instructions when relying on a single global injection policy.
AI.method: FARI categorizes MMDiT blocks into spatial anchoring, pre-activation, semantic, and late refinement blocks, applying selective feature transfer in anchoring and refinement blocks while incorporating all source features in pre-activation and semantic blocks according to the edit instruction type.
AI.result: Experiments on a newly curated benchmark and PIE-Bench show that FARI achieves favorable preservation-editability trade-offs across five edit instruction types.
AI.conclusion: Aligning feature injection policies with the functional specialization of MMDiT blocks provides interpretable, task-adaptive control for training-free image editing.

title: Unveiling Silent Hill with HeteroDiff: Dense Haze Removal via Heterogeneous Diffusion

AI.tldr: This paper proposes HeteroDiff, a heterogeneous diffusion framework for dense haze removal that combines curriculum learning, depth priors, and context-aware sampling. It outperforms state-of-the-art methods on NH-HAZE and DENSE-HAZE.
AI.motivation: Existing diffusion-based dehazing methods overlook the spatially heterogeneous restoration difficulty of dense haze, leading to imbalanced optimization and unstable generation.
AI.method: HeteroDiff introduces an Interleaved Curriculum Learning (ICL) strategy scheduling haze densities and diffusion timesteps from easy to hard, a Depth-Enhanced Noise Predictor (DENP) incorporating depth priors, and a Context-Aware Sampling (CAS) strategy to suppress hallucinated artifacts.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on NH-HAZE and DENSE-HAZE demonstrate that HeteroDiff consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in both visual quality and downstream object detection, especially under severe haze.
AI.conclusion: Accounting for heterogeneous haze density through curriculum scheduling and depth-guided diffusion substantially improves dense haze removal.

title: Hierarchical Visual Feature Fusion for Robust Out‐of‐Distribution Detection under Semantic and Image‐Level Covariate Shifts

AI.tldr: This paper proposes AFDisc, a unified out-of-distribution (OOD) detection framework that fuses shallow appearance-sensitive features and deep semantic features to detect both semantic and image-level covariate shifts.
AI.motivation: Existing OOD detection methods focus primarily on semantic novelty and struggle to detect image-level covariate shifts (such as noise, blur, or illumination changes) or settings where semantic and covariate shifts coexist.
AI.method: AFDisc uses an attentive fusion module to adaptively integrate shallow appearance-sensitive layers with deep semantic layers, trained with auxiliary supervision generated via controlled appearance perturbations.
AI.result: Extensive experiments under semantic shift, covariate shift, and combined shift settings demonstrate superior OOD detection performance over prior state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: Attentively fusing hierarchical visual features with perturbation-based auxiliary supervision provides robust OOD detection across diverse distribution shifts.

title: Adaptive Reference Refinement for Physics‐based Motion Retargeting

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a physics-based motion retargeting framework that uses a motion refinement network and a warmed-up reinforcement learning (RL) policy to produce physically plausible reference trajectories across differing morphologies.
AI.motivation: Kinematic retargeting ignores real-world dynamics such as gravity, contact forces, and torque limits, causing physical artifacts like foot sliding and ground penetration when guiding RL character control policies.
AI.method: A motion refinement network adjusts kinematically retargeted motions to be physically plausible, trained with a warming-up scheme that first fixes the refinement network while training the RL policy and then gradually introduces selective refinement offsets where substantial deviations occur.
AI.result: Experiments show consistent improvements in physical plausibility and tracking performance over inverse-kinematics baselines, with strong generalization across extreme limb-length changes and heavy payloads.
AI.conclusion: Coupling a selective motion refinement network with warmed-up RL training bridges kinematic retargeting and physically valid character control across diverse morphologies.

title: PanoLoop: Yaw‐Invariant Loop Closure for Feed‐Forward Panoramic SLAM

AI.tldr: This paper presents PanoLoop, a feed-forward panoramic SLAM system with yaw-invariant loop closure that uses candidate-stage suppression before multi-signal geometric verification. It produces globally consistent panoramic reconstructions on 360Loc.
AI.motivation: Feed-forward SLAM systems struggle on 360-degree panoramas because standard place descriptors fail under arbitrary revisit headings, while yaw-invariant descriptors generate a flood of false-positive candidates that overwhelm per-candidate geometric verifiers.
AI.method: PanoLoop introduces a yaw-invariant descriptor (YIP) based on Fourier magnitudes and adopts a sparsify-then-verify pipeline where candidate-stage suppression filters the candidate flood before a multi-signal verifier (MSV) judges the remaining candidates prior to pose-graph optimization.
AI.result: On the 360Loc benchmark, PanoLoop turns near-non-functional panoramic loop closure into an effective one, improving camera tracking over a strong panoramic visual-odometry baseline and yielding globally consistent reconstructions.
AI.conclusion: Suppressing false candidates early before geometric verification is key to enabling reliable yaw-invariant loop closure in feed-forward panoramic SLAM.

title: An Electrostatic Field‐Driven Method for Point Cloud Normal Orientation

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an electrostatic field-driven method for point cloud normal orientation using a dynamic, grid-free collection of discrete Coulomb particles. It produces globally coherent normal orientations while preserving fine geometric details.
AI.motivation: Existing point cloud normal orientation methods either propagate local orientations and risk global inconsistency, or solve global optimizations on pre-discretized grids that limit geometric flexibility.
AI.method: The method models normal orientation as an electrostatic field of discrete Coulomb kernels with closed-form expressions, optimizing particle positions, magnitudes, and counts dynamically so the resulting vector field is orthogonal to local tangent planes.
AI.result: Experiments across representative 3D models demonstrate that the formulation yields globally coherent normal orientations while preserving fine geometric details.
AI.conclusion: A dynamic, grid-free electrostatic particle field provides a flexible and globally consistent formulation for point cloud normal orientation.

title: Cage‐Based Dynamic Mesh Compression

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a cage-based dynamic mesh compression method that decomposes a mesh sequence into a static average mesh and a dynamic control cage using inverse cage-based animation. It outperforms direct dynamic mesh compression at high compression rates.
AI.motivation: Compressing dynamic mesh sequences directly becomes inefficient at high compression rates, and standard representations do not easily separate static shape from motion for downstream editing.
AI.method: Using mean value coordinates, the method approximates a mesh sequence by deforming its average mesh with a motion-aware dynamic cage, automatically constructing and optimizing the cage and compressing the static average mesh and dynamic cage sequence with existing codecs.
AI.result: At practically relevant high compression rates, the pipeline achieves better rate-distortion performance than direct dynamic mesh compression while also enabling sequence-wide shape editing by modifying the average mesh.
AI.conclusion: Inverse cage-based animation provides an effective, editable decomposition for high-ratio dynamic mesh compression.

title: LiteTex‐GS: Fast and Lightweight Texturing for Gaussian Splatting

AI.tldr: This paper proposes LiteTex-GS, a lightweight texturing framework for 2D Gaussian Splatting that progressively allocates texture resolution only to high-error primitives. It achieves competitive or superior novel-view synthesis quality with fewer parameters and faster training.
AI.motivation: Attaching texture maps to 2D Gaussians reduces primitive counts for high-frequency details, but complex parameterizations between discrete Gaussians and continuous 2D grids introduce heavy computational and memory overhead.
AI.method: LiteTex-GS initializes minimal local textures per Gaussian and progressively upsamples resolution only on primitives with high reconstruction error, paired with contribution- and area-aware pruning and a resolution-aware update rule to prevent gradient dilution.
AI.result: Experiments on standard novel view synthesis benchmarks show competitive or superior rendering quality using substantially fewer parameters and less training time than existing textured Gaussian baselines.
AI.conclusion: Error-driven progressive texture allocation and resolution-aware updates restore the training speed and compactness of Gaussian Splatting for detailed textured scenes.

title: Learning Discrete Riemannian Metric for Problem Aware Meshing

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a supervised learning method that predicts discrete Riemannian metric fields encoded as edge lengths to provide a warm-start initial mesh for Adaptive Mesh Refinement (AMR) in steady-state elliptic PDEs.
AI.motivation: Standard posterior-based AMR requires a good initial mesh for its first cold-start solve, while predicting metric tensor coefficients directly suffers from tangent-basis dependence on curved surfaces.
AI.method: The method encodes the Riemannian metric field via discrete edge lengths on fixed curved surfaces and trains a model on a solver-agnostic synthetic dataset of pre-solved PDE instances to predict the metric directly from source terms or constraints.
AI.result: On Poisson problems across three test domains, predicted metric-guided meshes reduce absolute discretization error by 27% to 43% compared to uniform meshes at matched resolution; on Obstacle problems, they achieve 2x to 3x faster convergence.
AI.conclusion: Learning basis-independent discrete edge-length metrics provides an effective warm start that accelerates existing AMR PDE solvers.

title: PropGesture: Few‐shot Co‐speech Gesture Synthesis for Handheld Props

AI.tldr: This paper presents PropGesture, a few-shot co-speech gesture synthesis framework for characters holding props that localizes object adaptation to the prop-holding arm using video-generated examples.
AI.motivation: Motion capture data cannot be collected at scale for every handheld prop, and naive few-shot conditioning or full-model finetuning either produces intermittent object awareness or loses gesture diversity.
AI.method: PropGesture synthesizes a small set of example clips via a video generation model, finetunes a phase-based arm motion generator on them to retrieve prop-specific arm motion via motion matching, and inpaints this arm motion into a pretrained gesture flow matching model for the rest of the body.
AI.result: Perceptual and quantitative comparisons against motion-example-based and finetuning-based baselines demonstrate improved prop-appropriate motion and preserved full-body gesture diversity.
AI.conclusion: Isolating few-shot prop adaptation to the holding arm and inpainting it into a pretrained full-body generator enables scalable, diverse co-speech gesture synthesis with handheld objects.

title: A Study of the Design Space of Motion and Disocclusion Control in Video Generation

AI.tldr: This paper systematically studies the design space of motion and disocclusion control in image-to-video generation across a new synthetic and captured benchmark. It finds that tracking-based guidance improves motion accuracy while image-based guidance improves revealed content fidelity.
AI.motivation: When object motion reveals previously hidden content (disocclusion), existing image-to-video methods offer various motion and disocclusion controls, but their trade-offs and design space remain poorly understood.
AI.method: The authors construct a benchmark of synthetic and captured scenes covering rigid/deformable motions and static/dynamic disoccluded objects, and evaluate existing and adapted methods across text-based vs. tracking-based motion control and text-based vs. image-based disocclusion control.
AI.result: Results show that tracking-based guidance yields higher motion accuracy and image-based guidance yields higher fidelity for newly revealed content, though jointly controlling the appearance and independent dynamics of disoccluded objects remains an open challenge.
AI.conclusion: This study clarifies the strengths and limitations of current control modalities for disocclusion in video generation and highlights joint appearance-dynamics control as a key future direction.

title: Fidelity‐preserved Visual Proxy Construction using Architectural Semantics

AI.tldr: This paper presents an automatic framework for constructing low-polygon visual proxies of buildings by extracting roof-top volumes and architectural semantics. It achieves higher perceptual fidelity and better feature preservation than geometric simplification baselines.
AI.motivation: Manual creation of low-polygon building proxies for city-scale rendering is labor-intensive, while automatic geometric simplification and plane-fitting methods ignore architectural semantics and distort key building mass features.
AI.method: The framework identifies vertically aligned functional sections via top-down ray casting and spatial segmentation, fits their boundaries and heights with primitives, extrudes them into roof-top volumes, and refines their sides laterally.
AI.result: Quantitative comparisons against three baselines on 40 buildings under similar face budgets and a 25-participant user study demonstrate higher perceptual fidelity, better architectural feature preservation, and competitive efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating architectural mass semantics enables automated generation of compact, perceptually faithful building proxies for large-scale 3D scenes.

title: A Frequency‐Decomposed Residual Learning Framework for Volume Data Neural Representation

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a frequency-decomposed residual learning framework for neural volume representation that models low-frequency components and high-frequency residuals via a shared implicit neural representation (INR) with feature gating.
AI.motivation: Existing INR-based volume representations suffer from spectral bias, struggling to capture fine high-frequency details needed for accurate scientific visualization and downstream analysis.
AI.method: The framework decomposes volume data into low-frequency components and high-frequency residuals, reformulating them as a multi-task learning problem with a shared INR backbone and a lightweight feature gating mechanism to adaptively reweight features and reduce branch conflicts.
AI.result: Experiments across multiple scientific datasets show consistent improvements over existing methods in reconstruction, super-resolution, and compression at comparable model size and computational cost, with ablations validating both decomposition and gating.
AI.conclusion: Frequency decomposition with adaptive feature gating mitigates spectral bias in INRs without sacrificing model compactness.

title: Image Vectorization with Generalized Coons Patches

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an image vectorization method using generalized Coons patches that represent images with shape-adaptive polygonal patches and error-driven interior control point insertion.
AI.motivation: Fixed-sided triangular or quadrilateral patches are inefficient for irregular or semantically complex image regions, requiring many small patches and suffering from fold-over issues.
AI.method: The method represents regions as shape-adaptive polygonal generalized Coons patches and introduces an error-driven adaptive refinement mechanism that inserts interior control points with fitted colors at high-error locations without re-partitioning patches or altering topology.
AI.result: Experimental results across diverse input images demonstrate high-quality image reconstruction using fewer patches and substantially fewer fold-over artifacts than conventional Coons patches.
AI.conclusion: Generalized Coons patches with topology-preserving interior refinement offer a flexible, compact representation for high-quality image vectorization.

title: MGAvatar: Mesh‐Bound Gaussians for Head Avatar Geometry and Appearance Modeling

AI.tldr: This paper proposes MGAvatar, a hybrid mesh-Gaussian representation for head avatars that transitions from vertex-bound Gaussians for geometry deformation to face-bound Gaussians with a view-conditioned neural color field for appearance modeling.
AI.motivation: Parametric head templates like FLAME lack personalized priors and struggle to represent complex structures such as hair and clothing in Gaussian-based head avatars.
AI.method: MGAvatar first uses constrained vertex-bound Gaussians and a pose-dependent offset module for progressive mesh deformation, then switches to face-bound Gaussians paired with a view-conditioned neural color field and an observation-space Gaussian offset network for dynamic textures.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on multi-view and monocular videos show that MGAvatar outperforms existing methods in rendering quality, producing high-fidelity head avatars with rich texture details.
AI.conclusion: Combining staged vertex- and face-bound Gaussians with view-conditioned neural colors enables expressive geometry and consistent dynamic appearance for head avatars.

title: Dream4D: Lifting Camera‐Controlled I2V towards Spatiotemporally Consistent 4D Generation

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Dream4D, a three-stage image-to-4D generation framework that pairs VLM-planned camera trajectories, pose-conditioned video diffusion, and 4D reconstruction to improve spatiotemporal consistency.
AI.motivation: Existing 4D generation methods lack broad 4D world knowledge, causing pose drift and temporal inconsistency in complex dynamic environments.
AI.method: Dream4D uses a vision-language model (VLM) to determine a camera trajectory from the input image and text instruction, generates geometrically consistent video frames along that trajectory with a pose-conditioned diffusion model, and reconstructs a persistent 4D representation from the generated video.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate that Dream4D significantly outperforms existing methods in both pose consistency and temporal consistency.
AI.conclusion: Combining VLM trajectory planning with pose-conditioned video diffusion and 4D reconstruction provides a strong pipeline for spatiotemporally consistent image-to-4D generation.

title: Camera Splatting for Continuous View Optimization

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Camera Splatting, a continuous view optimization framework that models cameras as 3D Gaussians (camera splats) to jointly optimize multiple views for novel view synthesis under limited camera budgets.
AI.motivation: Existing view selection methods choose from predefined camera sets or use greedy next-best-view strategies, limiting optimization flexibility and accuracy under tight camera budgets.
AI.method: Camera Splatting represents each camera as a specialized 3D Gaussian (camera splat) in continuous parameter space and places virtual point cameras at sampled scene points to render the splats and provide gradient feedback on view positions and orientations within a Gaussian splatting pipeline.
AI.result: Quantitative and qualitative evaluations demonstrate that Camera Splatting efficiently optimizes large numbers of views simultaneously and improves novel view synthesis under limited camera budgets.
AI.conclusion: Treating cameras as differentiable 3D Gaussian splats enables scalable, continuous joint view optimization for radiance field reconstruction.

title: Reliability‐Aware Adaptive Gaussian Propagation for Low‐Texture Dynamic Outdoor Scenes

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Reliability-Aware Adaptive Gaussian Propagation (RAGP) for 3D Gaussian Splatting in dynamic outdoor scenes with large low-texture regions, reducing artifacts and improving reconstruction fidelity.
AI.motivation: Binary foreground masking in dynamic outdoor 3DGS fails when dynamic boundaries corrupt static optimization and large low-texture areas like roads and walls lack reliable matching cues.
AI.method: RAGP adapts patch scales based on local structure and static reliability for pixel-level propagation, and fuses dynamic probability maps with rendering residuals into continuous reliability weights that constrain supervision, propagation filtering, and densification.
AI.result: Experiments on dynamic outdoor benchmarks show that RAGP reduces artifacts and erroneous densification while improving low-texture reconstruction and rendering fidelity.
AI.conclusion: Converting dynamic priors into continuous static reliability constraints within geometric propagation is more effective than binary masking for dynamic, low-texture outdoor scenes.

title: Bijective Shape Correspondence through Nonlinear Spectral Embedding Alignment

AI.tldr: This paper proposes the Bijective Neural Adjoint Map (BNAM), which bridges bidirectional Neural Adjoint Maps under a soft invertibility constraint with an iterative upsampling pipeline to achieve accurate, bijective 3D shape correspondence.
AI.motivation: Neural Adjoint Maps (NAM) are unidirectional and cannot guarantee bijectivity, while existing reciprocal spectral alignment methods implicitly assume isometric mappings and degrade on non-isometric shapes.
AI.method: BNAM couples two bidirectional NAMs with a soft invertibility constraint to encourage mutual bijectivity without imposing isometric priors, and uses an iterative upsampling pipeline for efficient estimation.
AI.result: Experiments show that BNAM promotes map bijectivity while preserving mapping accuracy across near-isometric, non-isometric, and unstructured point cloud scenarios.
AI.conclusion: Enforcing soft invertibility between bidirectional nonlinear spectral maps enables accurate, bijective correspondence even under challenging non-isometric deformations.

title: Scalable Capacity‐Constrained Power Diagrams via Compressed Optimal Assignment

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an exact algorithm for discrete capacity-constrained optimal assignment in large-scale sampled power diagrams, achieving one to two orders of magnitude speedup over classical methods.
AI.motivation: Capacity-constrained power diagrams are repeatedly solved in Lloyd-type geometry processing, but general-purpose minimum-cost flow solvers are slow and entropic-regularized approximations sacrifice exactness.
AI.method: Exploiting the asymmetry m << n between m sites and n samples, the algorithm performs augmentations on a compressed auxiliary graph of m + 2 nodes while maintaining point-level transfer costs in priority queues, projecting augmenting paths to bounded-length walks in O(nm^2 log n) time.
AI.result: Experiments on synthetic data and geometry-processing tasks show one to two orders of magnitude speedup over classical algorithms while preserving exact optimality for the discrete transport problem.
AI.conclusion: The method enables efficient, exact computation of capacity-constrained power diagrams in large-scale sampled settings.

title: OrnaStyler : Ornament‐Aware Latent Editing for Content‐Preserving 3D Stylization

AI.tldr: This paper presents OrnaStyler, a zero-shot framework for text-guided ornament-aware 3D stylization that preserves source geometry while integrating fine-grained stylistic details.
AI.motivation: Existing 3D stylization methods struggle to add fine-grained structural ornamentation without distorting the source geometry and object identity.
AI.method: Built on rectified flow generative modeling, OrnaStyler uses staged inversion-guided latent editing: it manipulates voxel representations via flow inversion for geometry augmentation and applies adjacency-aware feature inpainting at the appearance level, operating solely at inference time.
AI.result: Experiments on generated and real-world 3D assets show that OrnaStyler achieves state-of-the-art performance in content preservation, style fidelity, and visual realism.
AI.conclusion: Explicit spatial modeling of stylistic elements at inference time resolves the tension between content preservation and ornament-rich 3D stylization.

title: FlySeek: Visibility‐Aware Viewpoint Planning for Adversarial Target Pursuit in Complex 3D Scenes

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Adversarial Dynamic Target Visual Navigation, the FlySeek-Bench benchmark, and FlySeek, a visibility-guided policy framework for UAV pursuit of evasive targets in complex 3D scenes.
AI.motivation: Existing aerial vision-language navigation and tracking systems focus on static goals or non-adversarial targets, failing when targets actively use scene structures to break line-of-sight.
AI.method: FlySeek combines predicted target hypotheses with semantic-geometric visibility and occlusion reasoning, coupling action-wise geometric priors with learned visual-language preferences for preemptive viewpoint selection.
AI.result: Experiments in simulated and real-data-reconstructed scenes on FlySeek-Bench show that FlySeek improves tracking robustness, visibility continuity, and pursuit success over representative AVLN, tracking, and planning baselines under severe occlusion and adversarial motion.
AI.conclusion: Moving from passive target following to visibility-driven viewpoint planning is essential for aerial pursuit in dynamic, occlusion-rich 3D environments.

title: Implicit Surface Tension for Incompressible SPH Fluids with Interface Classification

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an implicit SPH surface tension solver that restricts cohesion forces and solver degrees of freedom to geometrically classified interface particles.
AI.motivation: Existing SPH surface tension solvers incur high computational costs and become unstable under strong surface tension effects.
AI.method: A geometric criterion using inter-particle distances and neighborhood angles classifies liquid-air interface, liquid-solid interface, and bulk particles without level sets or air-phase particles, then restricts volumetric cohesion and the implicit solve to interface particles with pressure-mediated force transfer.
AI.result: Experiments show the method significantly reduces computational cost, reproduces surface-tension-induced fluid effects, and mitigates excessive local cohesion in canonical scenarios.
AI.conclusion: Interface-restricted implicit solving provides a stable and efficient approach to simulating strong surface tension in incompressible SPH fluids.

title: EvoGS: Modeling Deformation Evolution for Dynamic Gaussian Splatting

AI.tldr: This paper proposes EvoGS, a dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that models Gaussian deformation as a temporal evolution process for novel view synthesis.
AI.motivation: Existing MLP-based dynamic 3DGS methods estimate deformations independently at each timestamp, making them less robust to large or abrupt motions.
AI.method: EvoGS maintains persistent deformation states per Gaussian, extrapolates future states from history, and corrects predictions with MLP observations weighted by temporal residual memory and evolution statistics, alongside deformation-aware and uncertainty-aware densification.
AI.result: Experiments across benchmarks show that EvoGS improves dynamic novel view synthesis quality and achieves competitive performance.
AI.conclusion: Modeling deformation as a stateful temporal evolution process enhances robustness and reconstruction quality in dynamic 3DGS.

title: A Survey of Modelling Temporal Coherence in Neural Rendering and Video Generation

AI.tldr: This survey systematically reviews and categorizes methods for modeling spatio-temporal coherence in neural rendering and generative AI video models.
AI.motivation: Unlike classic rendering with full pre-existing scene models, neural rendering and generative video models lack a shared scene representation and often suffer from spatial and temporal inconsistencies.
AI.method: The survey groups the literature into six categories based on how temporal information is introduced, represented, reused, or enforced: temporal interaction within the model, temporally coherent representations, temporally coherent guidance, temporal context propagation and reuse, temporally structured diffusion noise, and temporal losses, correction, and smoothing.
AI.result: It details the main characteristics of methods in each category, summarizes quality metrics used to evaluate temporal coherence, and outlines future research directions.
AI.conclusion: The taxonomy and metric overview provide a structured foundation for advancing temporal coherence in neural rendering and video generation.

title: Q‐MAGIC: Quad‐only Mesh Autoregressive Generation via Singularity‐Aware Circular Relative Offset Tokenization

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Q-MAGIC, an autoregressive Transformer model for quad-only mesh generation using singularity-aware serialization and circular relative offset tokenization.
AI.motivation: Autoregressive triangle mesh generation does not directly transfer to quad-only meshes because quad faces impose stricter topological and wiring constraints for unambiguous deserialization.
AI.method: Q-MAGIC introduces a singularity-aware serialization scheme that prioritizes wiring from singular points to shorten sequences, paired with circular relative offset tokenization that encodes geometry via local relative offsets for next-token prediction.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that Q-MAGIC produces more compact sequences while consistently improving geometric fidelity and mesh quality over state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: Topology-aware serialization and local relative offset tokenization enable effective autoregressive generation of quad-only meshes.

title: S2C2Seg++: Training-Free Category-Space Selection with Semantic-Spatial Fusion for Open-Vocabulary Segmentation

AI.tldr: This paper introduces S2C2Seg++, a training-free, plug-in framework for open-vocabulary semantic segmentation that couples adaptive category-space selection with semantic-spatial fusion in a closed inference-time loop, achieving 4.1 to 10.9 mIoU gains across baselines.
AI.motivation: Vision-language models like CLIP struggle with dense open-vocabulary segmentation due to large-vocabulary category redundancy and inconsistency between global semantics and local spatial precision, while existing methods typically fix the candidate category set in preprocessing.
AI.method: The framework combines Category Subset Selection (CSS) to distill the vocabulary using global semantic alignment, local spatial presence, and cross-view confidence, with Consistent Semantic Guidance (CSG) to modulate dense spatial evidence by per-category confidence; S2C2Seg++ further adds an iterative CSS-CSG feedback loop and score-gap-based adaptive cardinality for per-image subset sizing.
AI.result: Across eight standard protocols (19 to 171 categories) and PC-459, the method delivers 4.1 to 10.9 mIoU gains over baselines, with CorrCLIP + S2C2Seg++ reaching 51.9% mIoU as the best among compared training-free methods under the reported protocol.
AI.conclusion: Formulating open-vocabulary segmentation as a closed-loop, adaptive category-space selection and fusion process provides a strong, training-free complement to spatial refinement.

title: Generative Point Cloud Registration With Match-ControlNet

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Generative Point Cloud Registration, using DepthMatch-ControlNet and LiDARMatch-ControlNet to synthesize cross-view consistent RGB images aligned with point clouds for geometry-color feature fusion.
AI.motivation: Point cloud registration can benefit from 2D visual textures, but requires generated images that maintain both 2D-3D geometric alignment and cross-view texture consistency.
AI.method: DepthMatch-ControlNet conditions on depth maps with a coupled conditional denoising scheme and coupled prompt guidance for perspective RGB synthesis, while LiDARMatch-ControlNet conditions on paired equirectangular range maps from 360-degree LiDAR scans to generate panoramic RGB images.
AI.result: Experiments on 3DMatch and ScanNet for depth-camera settings and Dur360BEV for LiDAR settings show that integrating the generated images improves existing registration methods.
AI.conclusion: Controllable 2D generative models can effectively bridge 2D texture priors and 3D geometry to boost point cloud registration.

title: Image Quality Assessment for Machine-oriented Communication

AI.tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive visual quality assessment framework, dataset, and CFA-MoE metric for machine-oriented communication systems.
AI.motivation: Multimodal LLM-based low-bandwidth communication targets downstream computer vision tasks rather than human viewers, yet lacks an accepted evaluation metric.
AI.method: The authors build a generative MLLM codec pipeline, construct a 12k-pair reference/distorted image dataset across physical channels, run 600k inferences with 50 vision models on 5 downstream tasks, benchmark 18 IQA methods, and propose a Mixture-of-Experts metric called CFA-MoE.
AI.result: Experiments show that existing IQA algorithms cannot accurately evaluate machine-oriented distortions, while CFA-MoE serves as a strong baseline on the new dataset.
AI.conclusion: The dataset and CFA-MoE baseline establish a foundation for evaluating and advancing machine-oriented visual communication.

title: SplatCo: Structure-View Collaborative Gaussian Splatting for Detail-Preserving Rendering of Large-Scale Unbounded Scenes

AI.tldr: This paper proposes SplatCo, a structure-view collaborative 3D Gaussian Splatting framework for detail-preserving rendering of large-scale unbounded scenes.
AI.motivation: Large-scale 3DGS methods struggle to balance global structural coherence with local detail fidelity and suffer from Gaussian redundancy that causes rendering artifacts.
AI.method: SplatCo combines a Cross-Structure Collaboration Module fusing global tri-planes with local context grids, a Cross-View Pruning Mechanism removing structurally inconsistent Gaussians, and a Structure-View Co-learning module aggregating structural and view gradients.
AI.result: Evaluations on 13 large-scale scenes including Mill-19, MatrixCity, Tanks & Temples, WHU, and custom aerial captures show SplatCo sets a new benchmark for high-fidelity rendering.
AI.conclusion: Jointly enforcing structural collaboration, view-consistent pruning, and co-learned gradients enables scalable, artifact-free 3DGS rendering in unbounded scenes.

title: Incremental Learning of Vision-Language Models via Task Subspace Projection and Dynamic LoRA

AI.tldr: The paper proposes TSP-DLoRA, combining Task Subspace Projection (TSP) and Dynamic Low Rank Adapter (DLoRA) for Multi-Domain Task-Incremental Learning (MTIL) of pre-trained vision-language models, and demonstrates its effectiveness across 11 datasets.
AI.motivation: Pre-trained vision-language models in MTIL face forgetting of old tasks, degraded zero-shot transfer, and underfitting of new tasks under privacy and memory constraints, while existing cross-task identification (CTI) modules confuse seen and unseen tasks and new-task adaptation (NTA) modules fail to adaptively balance performance and parameter cost.
AI.method: The proposed TSP-DLoRA method pairs a Task Subspace Projection (TSP) module, which uses a task identifier classifier based on task-specific subspaces and a feature projection strategy to identify samples from both seen and unseen tasks, with a Dynamic Low Rank Adapter (DLoRA) module that dynamically assigns LoRA across transformer layers according to task distributions.
AI.result: Experimental evaluations across 11 datasets using three performance metrics demonstrate the effectiveness of TSP-DLoRA.
AI.conclusion: TSP-DLoRA provides an effective and efficient solution for MTIL in pre-trained vision-language models by improving seen/unseen task identification and adaptive parameter-efficient new-task learning.

title: GraphBEV++: Multi-Modal Feature Alignment for Autonomous Driving

AI.tldr: This paper proposes GraphBEV++, a multi-modal BEV feature alignment framework that mitigates sensor calibration and projection misalignment in autonomous driving.
AI.motivation: Calibration uncertainties between LiDAR and camera sensors cause projection-induced feature misalignment in BEV perception and end-to-end autonomous driving.
AI.method: GraphBEV++ pairs LocalAlign-v2, which uses neighborhood-aware depth features via graph matching for both LSS-based and query-based BEV, with GlobalAlign-v2, offering Deformable offset learning for LSS-based BEV and Diffusion denoising for query-based BEV.
AI.result: GraphBEV++ achieves state-of-the-art performance under misalignment noise on nuScenes and Waymo subset, improves long-range detection on Argoverse2, boosts 3D occupancy prediction, and outperforms UniAD, VAD, FusionAD, MomAD, and WoTE on open-loop (nuScenes) and closed-loop (Bench2Drive, NAVSIM) evaluations.
AI.conclusion: Explicit local and global cross-modal feature alignment significantly improves perception, prediction, and planning robustness under sensor misalignment.

title: WARM-CAT: Warm-Started Test-Time Comprehensive Knowledge Accumulation for Compositional Zero-Shot Learning

AI.tldr: This paper proposes WARM-CAT, a test-time adaptation framework for compositional zero-shot learning (CZSL), along with a new C-Fashion benchmark and a refined MIT-States dataset.
AI.motivation: Existing CZSL methods suffer from test-time label-space distribution shifts caused by unseen attribute-object compositions.
AI.method: WARM-CAT accumulates unsupervised textual and visual knowledge at test time with an adaptive update weight, uses a warm-started dynamic priority queue of high-confidence images for visual prototypes, and aligns textual and visual prototypes via multimodal collaborative representation learning.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that WARM-CAT achieves state-of-the-art performance on four benchmark datasets under both closed-world and open-world settings.
AI.conclusion: Warm-started test-time prototype accumulation and multimodal alignment effectively mitigate distribution shifts in CZSL.

title: Decoupling Latent 3D Facial Structure for Largely Masked Face Image Inpainting

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a two-stage face image inpainting framework that decouples and leverages latent 3D facial geometry and canonical texture to restore largely masked faces with strong identity preservation.
AI.motivation: Existing largely masked face inpainting methods primarily rely on remaining 2D pixels to complete missing regions, overlooking valuable 3D facial structure and spatial priors.
AI.method: The framework consists of a facial structure estimator with an ID consistency constraint that decouples 3D facial geometry and canonical-view texture, a Transformer-based preliminary inpainting module that integrates geometry restoration to complete facial priors, and a fine inpainting module that uses these priors and canonical texture constraints to guide up-sampling.
AI.result: Experiments show favorable inpainting performance on CelebA-HQ and competitive performance on FFHQ, particularly in preserving facial identity.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling and incorporating latent 3D facial geometry and canonical texture into a two-stage inpainting pipeline effectively improves structural authenticity, texture coherence, and identity preservation for largely masked face images.

title: Accelerated Online Risk-Averse Policy Evaluation in POMDPs with Theoretical Guarantees and Novel CVaR Bounds

AI.tldr: This paper presents a framework for accelerating online Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) policy evaluation in POMDPs using simplified surrogate dynamics with formal performance guarantees.
AI.motivation: Evaluating risk measures such as CVaR of cumulative returns in POMDPs is computationally demanding under partial observability.
AI.method: The authors derive CVaR bounds via a truncation decomposition separating an O(1/sqrt(n)) data-driven term from an O(1/n) tail correction, tighten them with local CDF concentration parameters, and apply them to simplified belief-MDPs for safe action elimination during online evaluation.
AI.result: Empirical evaluations across multiple POMDP domains show the bounds reliably distinguish safe from dangerous policies while achieving 9-21x computational speedups.
AI.conclusion: Surrogate-based CVaR bounding with action elimination provides a principled and practical speedup for risk-averse POMDP planning.

title: Learning Consensus Graph From Cross-Temporal Spectral Embeddings for Incremental Multiview One-Step Discrete Clustering

AI.tldr: This paper proposes IMDSC, an incremental multiview discrete spectral clustering method that jointly optimizes consensus graph construction, spectral embedding, and cluster label prediction.
AI.motivation: Conventional clustering requires full recomputation on data updates, while existing incremental methods separate view fusion from discrete label generation, causing error accumulation.
AI.method: IMDSC builds a consensus affinity matrix from cross-temporal spectral embeddings with graph regularization, and uses an orthogonal rotation matrix to suppress embedding drift and align embeddings directly with discrete cluster indicators without k-means postprocessing.
AI.result: Comparative experiments on multiple public benchmark datasets show that IMDSC outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both clustering accuracy and computational efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Unified incremental optimization with orthogonal rotation alignment eliminates postprocessing errors and improves dynamic multiview clustering.

title: Guided Continual Reinforcement Learning for Navigation via Integrative Consolidation and Memory Augmentation

AI.tldr: This paper proposes GCRL-ICMA, a knowledge-guided continual reinforcement learning framework for mobile robot navigation across incremental scenarios.
AI.motivation: Standard RL assumes fixed task distributions and suffers catastrophic forgetting, while existing parameter consolidation methods introduce bias that limits cross-scenario navigation.
AI.method: GCRL-ICMA combines elastic weight consolidation (EWC) and synaptic intelligence (SI) for parameter importance estimation, uses dual experience replay mixing current and clustered historical successful experiences, and adds a knowledge-guided module to reduce negative interference.
AI.result: Experiments on incremental multiscenario navigation tasks show that GCRL-ICMA alleviates forgetting, improves cross-scenario adaptability, and enhances learning efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Integrating complementary parameter consolidation, dual replay, and knowledge guidance improves continual RL navigation.

title: PointSARShip: Slice-Guided Point Supervision for Oriented SAR Ship Detection

AI.tldr: This paper proposes PointSARShip, an end-to-end point-supervised framework for oriented ship detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery.
AI.motivation: Horizontal bounding box annotations for SAR ship detection are labor-intensive, while cheap point annotations lack boundary and orientation cues.
AI.method: PointSARShip combines a slice-guided self-supervised learning strategy using ship slices as structural priors, a multi-scale spatial attention (MSSA) mechanism for varying ship sizes, and self-supervised viewpoint transformation training to model boundaries and orientations.
AI.result: Experiments on two SAR ship detection benchmarks show PointSARShip outperforms state-of-the-art point-supervised methods and narrows the gap to HBox- and fully-supervised methods.
AI.conclusion: Slice-guided structural priors and viewpoint-transformation self-supervision make low-cost point supervision viable for oriented SAR ship detection.

title: PGWS: A Prototype-Guided Weakly Supervised Framework for White Cashmere Goat Detection Under Extremely Sparse Annotations

AI.tldr: This paper proposes PGWS, a prototype-guided weakly supervised label-completion framework for white cashmere goat detection under extremely sparse annotations, improving mAP50 and recall without altering final detector inference.
AI.motivation: Annotating complete bounding boxes in dense, occluded breeding-farm images is costly, and extremely sparse annotations leave many foreground instances unlabeled so they are treated as background during training, weakening supervision.
AI.method: PGWS learns prototypes from available annotated objects to select additional foreground labels offline; teacher candidates are refined via class-wise prototype similarity and non-maximum suppression, then merged with sparse annotations under a ground-truth-first rule.
AI.result: Across three training runs on the White Cashmere Goat Dataset, PGWS achieves the highest mean mAP50 and recall among compared sparse-annotation methods (with a small mean mAP50 margin over Calibrated Teacher), ablations show label completion drives most of the gain, and supplementary tests cover a public tomato dataset and additional detector architectures.
AI.conclusion: Offline prototype-guided label completion offers a practical way to strengthen supervision under extremely sparse annotations while keeping final detector inference unchanged.

title: ScoutGS: Surrogate-Guided Optimization for 2D Gaussian Splatting Image Representation and Compression

AI.tldr: This paper proposes ScoutGS, a 2D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS) image representation and compression framework using prior-guided patch-level Rate-Distortion (RD) allocation.
AI.motivation: Existing 2DGS image methods allocate primitives via heuristic posterior errors and use global uniform quantization, leading to slow convergence and poor adaptive bitrate control.
AI.method: ScoutGS partitions images with a content-adaptive quadtree, pre-trains a dual-stream RD surrogate to assign initial Gaussian budgets, and runs a global Lagrangian search for patch-wise quantization profiles at a target bitrate while keeping the standard 2DGS decoder.
AI.result: On Kodak with 5K primitives, ScoutGS converges 38% faster than 2DGS baselines; under target compression ratios on Kodak, it achieves a 0.93 dB BD-PSNR gain and 24.45% BD-rate reduction while keeping realized bitrate within 8% of the target, and also outperforms baselines on DIV2K.
AI.conclusion: Surrogate-guided RD allocation and patch-wise quantization enable fast, bitrate-controllable 2DGS image compression without modifying the decoder.

title: Beyond Sensing Fragility: Complementary-Pathway Distillation for Robust Depth Estimation

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a complementary-pathway distillation framework that transfers RGB depth foundation-model priors into dual-pathway Complementary Vision Sensors (CVS).
AI.motivation: RGB depth foundation models are fragile to motion blur and exposure failure, whereas CVS decouple slow semantic and high-speed structural pathways but suffer from a modality gap and limited training data.
AI.method: The framework transfers RGB foundation-model priors into the dual-pathway CVS representation using asymmetric cross-modal alignment to inject semantic context into high-speed structural features and progressive distillation for stability under degraded inputs.
AI.result: Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets show robust depth estimation at a 757-FPS equivalent temporal resolution, maintaining 0.26 Abs Rel under severe imaging degradations.
AI.conclusion: Complementary-pathway distillation bridges brain-inspired sensing and vision foundation models for high-speed, degradation-robust depth estimation.

title: Beyond Symmetric Alignment: Asymmetric Causal Interventions for Event-Driven Financial Forecasting

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Causal Market-State Generation (CMSG), a multimodal framework that formalizes financial news as a causal do-calculus intervention on 2D K-line charts.
AI.motivation: Existing multimodal financial forecasting models treat news text and market charts symmetrically, conflating causal news impacts with spurious correlations from unobserved market inertia.
AI.method: CMSG uses vision spatial priors to locate news-sensitive chart regions, applies a Vector Quantization-based Causal Tokenizer to decompose them into endogenous inertia and an exogenous intervention residual, and uses a contrastive objective over factual and counterfactual attention maps for Individual Treatment Effect estimation.
AI.result: On Quant-MM (2,500 macro-news events paired with K-line charts from Nov 2024 to Mar 2026), CMSG outperforms 12 baselines, achieving 46.85% Macro-F1 (4.75% above the strongest time-series SOTA) and a 4.8522 Information Ratio.
AI.conclusion: Asymmetric causal decomposition of news interventions and market inertia improves event-driven financial forecasting.

title: DEAL: Deep Evidential Audio-Visual Learning for Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection

AI.tldr: This paper proposes DEAL, a Deep Evidential Audio-Visual Learning framework for weakly supervised video anomaly detection under temporal asynchrony and modality noise.
AI.motivation: Existing audio-visual WS-VAD methods fail to measure modality reliability, leading to blind fusion of noisy or temporally misaligned modalities.
AI.method: DEAL integrates a State Space Model-based Feature Extraction and Alignment (FEA) module with cross-modal parameter exchange, a Bi-Branch Deep-Evidential Fuser (BDF) using Evidential Neural Networks for uncertainty-based re-weighting, and Joint-Modal Mutual Learning (JML) to calibrate overconfidence.
AI.result: Experiments on XD-Violence show that DEAL suppresses noise, achieves semantic alignment without timestamp supervision, and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: Explicit epistemic uncertainty modeling and dynamic cross-modal alignment eliminate blind fusion in multimodal video anomaly detection.

title: Unified Multimodal Model Proficient in Continued Training

AI.tldr: This paper proposes MEANING, a unified multimodal model that prevents catastrophic forgetting during continued post-pre-training without original pre-training data.
AI.motivation: Continued training of unified understanding-and-generation multimodal models without pre-training data causes severe catastrophic forgetting and cross-task interference.
AI.method: MEANING introduces Dual Layer-Level LoRA Routing with modality-specific routers to sparsely activate LoRA adapters, paired with a Layer-Routed Attention Distillation loss that aligns internal reasoning patterns within active layers.
AI.result: Experiments across understanding, generation, and editing tasks show MEANING prevents the average 60.1% performance drop seen in naive continued training and improves both faculties.
AI.conclusion: Sparse layer-level routing combined with targeted attention distillation enables stable continued training of unified multimodal models.

title: Investigating the Robustness of Multi-Model Driving Perception to a Joint Physical Patch

AI.tldr: This demo presents a live physical adversarial-patch system that simultaneously disrupts optical flow, monocular depth estimation, and semantic segmentation in camera-based driving perception.
AI.motivation: Autonomous driving relies on dense multi-task perception pipelines, yet physical adversarial robustness is typically evaluated on isolated models rather than joint pipelines.
AI.method: A single printable road patch is optimized in the latent space of a diffusion model for visual plausibility and cross-task adversarial impact, then tested live on a robot car streaming video to RAFT, Depth-Anything-v2, and PSPNet.
AI.result: Real-time demonstrations show synchronized perception failures across all three models as the physical patch enters the camera's view.
AI.conclusion: The demo underscores the need to evaluate physical adversarial robustness at the multi-task perception pipeline level.

title: DART: Difficulty-Aware Adaptive Reasoning for Music Information Retrieval
