AI.tldr: This paper proposes DART, a difficulty-aware adaptive reasoning framework for music information retrieval (MIR), along with re-annotated benchmarks CLEAR-MusicTags and ExpertEval-MusicTags.
AI.motivation: MIR requires balancing low-level acoustic perception and high-level semantic reasoning, where over-deliberation causes hallucinations, under-reasoning yields shallow predictions, and benchmark noise hinders training.
AI.method: DART introduces CLEAR-MusicTags (LLM-assisted consensus re-annotation) and ExpertEval-MusicTags, trains Rubric-guided Adaptive Thinking via GRPO to calibrate reasoning invocation, and identifies internal difficulty activation directions for inference-time steering without retraining.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show DART achieves state-of-the-art performance on refined benchmarks and transfers promisingly zero-shot to other MIR tasks.
AI.conclusion: Difficulty-aware adaptive reasoning and activation steering provide interpretable, high-performing music understanding.

title: Internal Token Compression with Lightweight Adaptation for High-Resolution Monocular Depth Models

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a lightweight adaptation framework using RepLoRA to recover accuracy in internal token-compressed ViT monocular depth models.
AI.motivation: High-resolution ViT depth models incur quadratic attention cost, while internal token compression degrades accuracy because later blocks and the decoder rely on spatially structured features.
AI.method: Tokens are compressed at an intermediate encoder stage, remaining blocks are adapted with RepLoRA (fusing linear and spatial convolution branches in qkv projections at inference), positional embeddings are tuned, and the decoder combines pre- and post-compression features using 200K pseudo-depth images.
AI.result: On NYUv2, KITTI, and DA-2K, RepLoRA recovers pooling degradation, reducing GFLOPs from 42.7 to 21.8-29.4, attention cost from 25.03M to 5.47M-13.29M, and boosting RTX 3080 TensorRT throughput from 76.3 FPS to 112.0-164.5 FPS.
AI.conclusion: Reparameterizable spatial-linear adaptation enables substantial speedups in ViT depth models without changing the input interface.

title: See No Evil: Aligning Vision-Language Agents with Multimodal Contextual Integrity via Adversarial Reinforcement Learning

AI.tldr: This paper formulates GUI agent privacy as Multimodal Contextual Integrity (M-CI) and proposes Visual-Agent Guardian (VAG) trained via Constrained GRPO and adversarial self-play.
AI.motivation: Text-centric safety guardrails treat privacy as a static entity property and fail for GUI Vision-Language Agents that can leak screen-embedded sensitive data through both text and grounded actions.
AI.method: VAG represents interaction states with a contextual tuple and region-level GUI authorization map, using counterfactual inverse rendering, an M-CI-CoT module, and a Visual-Semantic Reward Model trained with Constrained GRPO (PID-Lagrangian updates) and adversarial self-play.
AI.result: Across three privacy-critical benchmarks, VAG reduces visual privacy leakage to under 5% while averaging over 80% task success, and lowers multimodal social-engineering attack success below 4%.
AI.conclusion: Operationalizing Multimodal Contextual Integrity with constrained RL substantially improves the privacy-utility Pareto frontier for GUI agents.

title: QTok: Scalable 1D Visual Tokenization via Decoupled Querying

AI.tldr: This paper proposes QTok, a decoupled "Encode-then-Query" 1D visual tokenizer that achieves linear scaling complexity and compatibility with pretrained foundation models.
AI.motivation: Existing 1D image tokenizers concatenate learnable latent tokens with image patches at the input, causing foundation-model incompatibility, quadratic complexity, and single-scale bottlenecks.
AI.method: QTok first extracts a Hierarchical Multi-Level Memory using a standard encoder, then distills it into compact latent tokens via a lightweight Query Attention Module using cross-attention.
AI.result: On ImageNet-1K, QTok sets a new state-of-the-art in generation fidelity, semantic consistency, and efficiency, achieving superior performance with only 50% of the standard training schedule when using pretrained encoders.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling encoding from querying enables scalable, foundation-model-compatible 1D visual tokenization.

title: Cognitively-Inspired Adaptive Reasoning for Multimodal Emotion Recognition

AI.tldr: This paper proposes CIAR, a three-stage Cognitively-Inspired Adaptive Reasoning framework for multimodal emotion recognition (MER).
AI.motivation: Existing adaptive reasoning methods for MER fail to model varying cognitive difficulty, leading to a trade-off between performance and efficiency.
AI.method: CIAR uses cold-start fine-tuning, models continuous cognitive difficulty via modality conflict and modality reliance, and optimizes the reasoning policy with difficulty-aware reinforcement learning using verifiable rewards.
AI.result: Experiments across multiple MER benchmarks in open- and closed-vocabulary settings show CIAR achieves a superior balance of performance and efficiency, strong out-of-domain generalization, and scalability.
AI.conclusion: Continuous cognitive difficulty modeling yields human-aligned, efficient reasoning for multimodal emotion recognition.

title: Bat Vocalization Explorer: An Interactive, Leakage-Controlled Tool for Decoding Behavioural Context from Egyptian Fruit Bat Calls

AI.tldr: This demo presents Bat Vocalization Explorer, an interactive browser-based tool for leakage-controlled decoding of behavioural context from Egyptian fruit bat calls.
AI.motivation: In-individual evaluation scores in animal vocalization decoding can be inflated by identity leakage, requiring transparent, leakage-controlled inspection.
AI.method: The self-contained browser tool pairs discrete tokenization with a live re-trainable linear probe, comparing in-individual vs. held-out cross-individual/cross-session macro-F1 and highlighting discrete situation markers.
AI.result: It exposes score inflation, identifies biting-context tokens (P > 0.85, ~8x over base rate), and reports that a classical mel front-end outperforms the BEATs audio foundation model on this ultrasonic corpus.
AI.conclusion: The tool makes leakage-controlled bioacoustic evaluation and discrete token analysis accessible and interactive in the browser.

title: SEPO: Self-Evolving Preference Optimization for Diffusion Alignment via Dynamic Rule Refinement

AI.tldr: This paper proposes SEPO, a Self-Evolving Preference Optimization framework that dynamically refines evaluation rules during diffusion model alignment.
AI.motivation: Static reward models and fixed datasets fail to adapt as diffusion models improve and alignment requirements shift toward finer-grained visual criteria.
AI.method: SEPO uses a multi-role agent system to evolve a natural language playbook through judgment, critique, and arbitration, and injects rule-based visual descriptions as augmented conditions during DPO training so the model internalizes them for inference with original prompts.
AI.result: Experiments in offline and online settings on SDXL and FLUX show SEPO achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving ImageReward by 15.4% and HPSv2 by 5.2%.
AI.conclusion: Dynamic rule refinement with conditional DPO semantic injection raises the alignment ceiling for text-to-image diffusion models.

title: UPR-VAD: U ncertainty-guided Signal P urification and R egularization for Weakly-Supervised V ideo A nomaly D etection

AI.tldr: This paper proposes UPR-VAD, an uncertainty-guided signal purification and regularization framework for weakly-supervised video anomaly detection (WSVAD).
AI.motivation: WSVAD suffers from intra-video ambiguity under coarse video-level labels, temporal granularity mismatch in vision-language guidance, and gradient saturation on hard anomaly patterns.
AI.method: UPR-VAD forms a co-evolutionary loop combining an Uncertainty-aware Temporal Information Bottleneck (U-TIB), Intra-Video Negative Contrastive Learning (IVNC) using shared uncertainty masks, and Sparsity-Guided Confidence Regularization (SGCR) with Sparsity Prior Alignment (SPA).
AI.result: Extensive experiments on widely used WSVAD benchmarks validate the effectiveness and superiority of UPR-VAD.
AI.conclusion: Coupling epistemic uncertainty suppression with contrastive hard-negative mining and confidence regularization improves weakly-supervised anomaly detection.

title: Rethinking Modality Balance: Strategic Asymmetry for Multimodal Domain Generalization

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Strategic Asymmetry, a multimodal domain generalization framework that prioritizes domain-stable modalities over rigid modality balance.
AI.motivation: Existing multimodal domain generalization methods enforce modality balance, which the authors show can loosen generalization bounds by forcing reliance on modalities sensitive to distribution shifts.
AI.method: Strategic Asymmetry uses a prototype-based Dynamic Stability Estimation module to quantify modality stability and a Stability-Guided Asymmetric Modulation mechanism to prioritize stable features while keeping unstable ones as bounded complementary signals.
AI.result: Evaluations across 28 transfer tasks demonstrate strong, competitive performance and robust gains under diverse distribution shifts.
AI.conclusion: Structurally favoring stable modalities over forced balance improves out-of-domain generalization in multimodal learning.

title: PACER: Parameter-Efficient Vision-Language Alignment with Class-Adaptive Calibration for Emotion Recognition

AI.tldr: This paper proposes PACER, a parameter-efficient vision-language alignment framework for driver emotion recognition using a frozen CLIP backbone.
AI.motivation: Unimodal visual methods lack discriminability, multimodal fusion adds deployment complexity, and naive CLIP adaptation either underutilizes priors or risks forgetting.
AI.method: PACER introduces Class-Adaptive Prompt Calibration to weight multiple driver-specific text prompts into class prototypes and Temporal-Aware Gated Aggregation to capture frame-level emotional dynamics, adding 10.5M trainable parameters (6.9% of CLIP) and 0.0297 GFLOPs.
AI.result: On AIDE-Emotion and RAVDESS, PACER outperforms state-of-the-art methods and achieves ~110 FPS inference on an NVIDIA Orin-X automotive platform.
AI.conclusion: Calibrated prompt prototypes and lightweight temporal aggregation enable real-time, parameter-efficient driver emotion recognition.

title: HRaLLM: Hyperbolic Rough Aware Large Language Model for Multimodal Action Reasoning

AI.tldr: This paper proposes HRaLLM, a multimodal large language model that uses hyperbolic skeleton manifold rough embeddings to complement defective images for action reasoning.
AI.motivation: Multimodal action reasoning suffers from background clutter, occlusions, and viewpoint changes, and existing methods often rely on image or skeleton data alone.
AI.method: HRaLLM introduces a rough tokenizer on a hyperbolic manifold to encode hierarchical 3D skeleton topologies, a skeleton-image complementary fusion module to reduce cross-modal hallucination, and a four-stage multimodal anticipation enhancement fine-tuning strategy.
AI.result: Extensive experiments and visualizations demonstrate that HRaLLM outperforms existing approaches across diverse action reasoning benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Hyperbolic skeleton tokenization and complementary image fusion enhance spatio-temporal action reasoning in MLLMs.

title: DP 2 -NeRF: Dual-Prior Probabilistic Neural Radiance Fields for Event-Guided Motion Deblurring

AI.tldr: This paper proposes DP2-NeRF, a dual-prior probabilistic NeRF framework for event-guided motion deblurring.
AI.motivation: Prior event-based 3D reconstruction methods rely solely on physics-based Event Double Integration (EDI) when forming explicit sharp-color priors, missing the noise-suppression benefits of learned priors.
AI.method: DP2-NeRF fuses physics-based EDI with a learning-based EICA prior and extends evidential uncertainty through spatial volumetric rendering and temporal blur formation to adaptively down-weight unreliable observations.
AI.result: Experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks show that DP2-NeRF outperforms existing event-enhanced 3D reconstruction methods under matched evaluation conditions.
AI.conclusion: Uncertainty-aware fusion of physics-based and learned event priors improves 3D reconstruction from motion-blurred images.

title: Proxy Information Bottleneck for Multi-modal Clustering

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Proxy Information Bottleneck (PIB), a unified information bottleneck framework for unsupervised multi-modal clustering.
AI.motivation: Existing IB-based multi-modal clustering methods optimize information preservation locally, failing to jointly align modality-specific features with global cluster assignments.
AI.method: PIB compresses each modality via variational encoders, constructs a global shared representation as proxy semantics through cross-modal alignment, and uses a conditional mutual information term optimized via variational inference and a Jensen-Shannon divergence estimator to capture task-beneficial modality-specific cues.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that PIB outperforms state-of-the-art multi-modal clustering approaches.
AI.conclusion: Using a globally fused representation as proxy semantics enables unified information-bottleneck optimization for multi-modal clustering.

title: LAMDA: Low-Rank Magnitude–Direction Adaptation for Class-Incremental Object Detection

AI.tldr: This paper proposes LAMDA, a Low-Rank Magnitude-Direction Adaptation framework for class-incremental object detection (CIOD).
AI.motivation: Directly applying LoRA to CIOD is suboptimal because sequential low-rank updates cause unmanaged parameter drift and background-dominated gradient bias.
AI.method: LAMDA decouples update magnitude and direction using a Low-Rank Pyramid (LoRP) that shrinks rank by task correlation, a Foreground-Centric Gradient Space (FCGS) to isolate object-relevant historical gradients, and Relaxed Gradient Projection (RGP) for positive transfer under co-occurrence.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on PASCAL VOC and MS COCO show LAMDA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, especially in long-sequence incremental settings.
AI.conclusion: Explicit magnitude-direction decoupling of low-rank updates mitigates forgetting and background bias in CIOD.

title: Unsupervised Incomplete Two-stage Cross-modal Hashing

AI.tldr: This paper proposes UITCH, an Unsupervised Incomplete Two-stage Cross-modal Hashing framework for multimedia retrieval with missing modalities and no labels.
AI.motivation: Existing cross-modal hashing methods assume complete, paired data or manual annotations, which rarely hold in real-world retrieval scenarios.
AI.method: Using CLIP features, UITCH first performs Semantic-Preserving Modality Reconstruction with a neural Cross-modal Mutual Information constraint, then performs Fusion-Guided Contrastive Hashing using a Mutually Enhanced Affinity Matrix Fusion strategy with a Cross-modal Transformer.
AI.result: Experiments on MIRFlickr, NUS-WIDE, and MS COCO show that UITCH significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines under incomplete and unsupervised settings.
AI.conclusion: Mutual-information-guided imputation and consensus affinity fusion enable effective unsupervised cross-modal hashing on incomplete data.

title: D 2 PO: Dual-Direction Preference Optimization via Adaptive Distribution Alignment for Vision-Language Models

AI.tldr: This paper proposes D2PO, a Dual-Direction Preference Optimization framework for mitigating hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs).
AI.motivation: Off-policy DPO in LVLMs suffers from unstable optimization due to mismatches between the evolving model policy and static preference data.
AI.method: D2PO combines an Adaptive Distribution Contraction (ADC) module to align generation distributions with high-quality regions and an Entropy-guided Hard Sample Discovery (EHSD) strategy to target hallucination-prone samples.
AI.result: On MMHalBench, ObjectHalBench, AMBER, and POPE Adv, D2PO outperforms DPO-based methods on 7B and 13B LVLMs using only 3.1K preference samples, reducing hallucination rates by 40-50%.
AI.conclusion: Adaptive distribution contraction and entropy-guided hard-sample selection provide sample-efficient hallucination mitigation for LVLMs.

title: MARS: Dynamic Feature Disentanglement via Manifold-Aligned Representation Splitting for Weakly-Supervised Domain Adaptive Object Detection

AI.tldr: This paper proposes MARS, a dynamic feature disentanglement framework for weakly-supervised domain adaptive (WSDA) object detection.
AI.motivation: Existing WSDA object detection methods globally align Domain-Invariant Attributes (DIA) but overlook Domain-Similarity Attributes (DSA) such as object contours and morphology.
AI.method: MARS uses Semantic Similarity Matching (SSM) to pair semantically similar images, Manifold-based Representation Splitting (MRS) with learnable gates to orthogonally decompose DIA and DSA, and Parallel Knowledge Mining (PKM) to extract knowledge from both.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across various transfer scenarios demonstrate that MARS achieves state-of-the-art performance.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling and mining both domain-invariant and domain-similarity attributes improves weakly-supervised domain adaptive object detection.

title: Tune Less, Erase Better: Angle-Guided Multi-Granularity Unlearning in Continual Learning

AI.tldr: This paper proposes CLgeU, an angle-guided multi-granularity unlearning framework for continual learning that avoids full fine-tuning and extra data storage.
AI.motivation: Existing continual learning with unlearning (CLU) methods lack multi-granularity support (sample, class, task), require costly full-model fine-tuning, and rely on storing extra historical data.
AI.method: CLgeU adds a lightweight unlearning module in the output space that shifts decision boundaries by selectively optimizing the target angle factor of decomposed logits, erasing target knowledge without replaying non-target data.
AI.result: Experiments on public benchmarks show CLgeU achieves effective, efficient unlearning across regularization-, replay-, and optimization-based CL strategies without harming retained or future tasks.
AI.conclusion: Output-space angle-guided logit perturbation enables lightweight, storage-free, multi-granularity unlearning in continual learning.

title: Language-Anchored Hierarchical Relational Distillation for Continual Multimedia Scene Parsing

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Language-Anchored Hierarchical Relational Distillation (LA-HRD) for continual panoptic segmentation, stabilizing scene representations across semantic, spatial, and instance levels. Experiments on ADE20K continual protocols and COCO show improved stability-plasticity trade-off and more coherent scene parsing over long incremental sequences.
AI.motivation: Existing continual panoptic segmentation methods rely on evolving visual features to preserve knowledge, which becomes fragile during long incremental learning and fails to maintain coherent semantic relations, spatial layouts, and instance-level distinctions.
AI.method: LA-HRD stabilizes representations at three levels: frozen language embeddings act as a semantic anchor for global class topology, visual distillation preserves spatial-contextual structure, and prototype-guided contrastive alignment improves instance-level compactness and temporal consistency.
AI.result: Experiments on multiple ADE20K continual protocols and additional COCO evaluation demonstrate that LA-HRD consistently improves the stability-plasticity trade-off and produces more coherent scene parsing results over long incremental sequences.
AI.conclusion: Aligning different forms of knowledge in their appropriate reference spaces enables more robust long-term continual multimodal scene understanding.

title: OpenDPC: An Open Source Dynamic Point Cloud Player and Platform for Just Noticeable Distortion

AI.tldr: This paper introduces OpenDPC, an open-source Unity-based platform for dynamic point cloud playback and subjective quality evaluation, along with a 60-subject just noticeable distortion (JND) experiment over 18 sequences.
AI.motivation: Open infrastructure for evaluating the perceptual quality of dynamic point clouds under compression has been lacking despite their potential in virtual reality and autonomous driving.
AI.method: OpenDPC provides a Unity-based playback and subjective evaluation platform with a JND annotation submodule that uses paired comparisons over a published 20-level V-PCC distortion ladder to identify the smallest perceptible distortion.
AI.result: A 60-subject subjective experiment across 18 dynamic point cloud sequences establishes a reproducible baseline, with software, encoder configurations, and test data released on GitHub and OpenI.
AI.conclusion: OpenDPC provides a reproducible open-source platform and baseline dataset for future perceptual quality and JND research on dynamic point clouds.

title: DvMF: Uncertainty-Aware Disentangled Representation Learning for Multi-View Clustering

AI.tldr: This paper proposes DvMF, a multi-view clustering framework that combines representation disentanglement with uncertainty-aware von Mises-Fisher (vMF) fusion, outperforming recent state-of-the-art methods on multiple benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing multi-view clustering methods often suffer from feature entanglement between view-shared semantics and view-specific variations, which reduces representation discriminability and degrades clustering performance.
AI.method: DvMF uses a tripartite mutual information objective to separate view-shared semantics from view-specific factors, projects the disentangled representations onto a hyperspherical latent space modeled by the vMF distribution, and fuses them via a Product-of-Experts mechanism weighted by vMF concentration parameters.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets show that DvMF consistently outperforms recent state-of-the-art multi-view clustering methods.
AI.conclusion: Combining mutual-information-based disentanglement with uncertainty-aware vMF hyperspherical fusion effectively mitigates noisy view-specific components and improves multi-view clustering.

title: Appearance-Semantic balanced 3D Feature Gaussian Representation

AI.tldr: This paper presents an appearance-semantic balanced 3D Gaussian Splatting representation that improves both 3D semantic scene understanding and high-fidelity visual reconstruction.
AI.motivation: Integrating appearance and semantic information into 3D Gaussian Splatting is difficult because fine-grained appearance requires dense primitives while semantic information is sparse and structured in 3D scenes.
AI.method: The framework introduces Decoupled Appearance Learning (DAL) to separate view-consistent base appearance from view-dependent effects, Multi-Attribute Consistency Consolidation (MACC) to prune redundant primitives while preserving intra-class diversity, and Adaptive Semantic-driven Densification (ASD) to redistribute primitives toward semantically informative regions.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that the proposed representation achieves improved reconstruction and segmentation performance.
AI.conclusion: Jointly exploiting semantic priors and appearance characteristics resolves the density mismatch in 3D Gaussian Splatting for more efficient 3D scene understanding.

title: IDC-RFT: Incentivizing Fine-Grained Image Difference Captioning via Reinforcement Fine-Tuning

AI.tldr: This paper proposes IDC-RFT, a rule-based reinforcement fine-tuning framework for Image Difference Captioning (IDC) that outperforms state-of-the-art methods across seven benchmarks.
AI.motivation: MLLM-based IDC methods struggle to generalize to unseen environments and novel change types, while applying rule-based RL faces ambiguous rewards for open-ended captions and inefficient difference perception policy learning.
AI.method: IDC-RFT introduces a dual-dimensional caption reward mechanism combining Multi-Change Structural Reward (MCSR) and Semantic Reward (SR), alongside a dual-modality contrastive optimization strategy using Text- and Vision-oriented Contrastive Difference Identification (T-CDI and V-CDI) as auxiliary tasks.
AI.result: Experiments across seven benchmarks show that IDC-RFT significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods using identical backbones.
AI.conclusion: Combining verifiable structural and semantic rewards with contrastive auxiliary tasks enables rule-based RL to learn more generalizable difference perception policies for IDC.

title: Full-tuning CLIP for Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Self-Supervised Distribution Alignment (SSDA) and SAM-based post-processing (SPP) to full-tune CLIP for Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation (WSSS), achieving state-of-the-art results on PASCAL VOC 2012 and competitive performance on MS COCO 2014.
AI.motivation: Existing CLIP-based WSSS methods keep CLIP frozen, leaving it unable to adapt to distribution shifts between CLIP pre-training data and downstream segmentation datasets.
AI.method: SSDA reconstructs the segmentation dataset into an image-text matching dataset using CLIP Surgery pseudo-labels for full-tuning CLIP with a Feature Rectification Loss L_FR, and SPP uses SAM-generated attention to suppress irrelevant regions during affinity propagation and refined pseudo-labels as SAM prompts.
AI.result: Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on PASCAL VOC 2012 and competitive results on MS COCO 2014.
AI.conclusion: Full-tuning CLIP with self-supervised distribution alignment and SAM-guided post-processing overcomes domain shift and produces finer pseudo-labels for WSSS.

title: Lifelong Gait Recognition via Prototype-guided Low-Rank Adaptive Distillation

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Lifelong Gait Recognition (LGR) and proposes Prototype-guided Low-Rank Adaptive Distillation (PLoRA), achieving state-of-the-art performance on CCPG and CASIA-B while introducing a new large-scale LGR benchmark.
AI.motivation: Existing gait recognition methods assume a stationary single-dataset domain and fail in continually changing real-world environments that require incremental learning across multiple domains.
AI.method: PLoRA combines a domain-specific LoRA module with a prototype-guided topology distillation module to mitigate catastrophic forgetting on seen domains and improve generalization to unseen domains.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that PLoRA achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming the joint-training baseline in Mean Rank-1 accuracy on CCPG and Rank-1 accuracy under the NM condition on CASIA-B.
AI.conclusion: Prototype-guided low-rank adaptive distillation enables continual cross-domain gait recognition without catastrophic forgetting and sets a new benchmark for LGR.

title: See to Act, Adapt to Act: Action-Stable Continual Test-Time Adaptation for Multimodal Embodied Intelligence

AI.tldr: This paper proposes See to Act, Adapt to Act, a Continual Test-Time Adaptation (CTTA) paradigm for multimodal embodied intelligence that prioritizes action stability and outperforms baselines by over 40% on the proposed ALOHA-C benchmark.
AI.motivation: Existing CTTA methods from pure vision rely on passive observational alignment, which corrupts kinematic representations, causes error accumulation, and leads to catastrophic forgetting of physical manipulation skills during continuous embodied execution.
AI.method: In the See to Act phase, the model extracts and decouples transient and steady features; in the Adapt to Act phase, a teacher-student architecture performs boundary-aware feature updating and adaptive action generation using steady or transient features as needed.
AI.result: Evaluations on the newly proposed closed-loop ALOHA-C benchmark show that the framework outperforms existing baselines across diverse dynamic scenarios, achieving performance gains of over 40% under multiple settings.
AI.conclusion: Robust embodied CTTA requires shifting from passive perceptual alignment to active action stability.

title: ConfAvatar: Confidence-Aware Self-Bootstrapping for Monocular 4D Head Avatar Reconstruction

AI.tldr: This paper proposes ConfAvatar, a confidence-aware self-bootstrapping framework for monocular 4D head avatar reconstruction that achieves state-of-the-art performance by guiding diffusion priors with view-dependent confidence maps.
AI.motivation: Applying generative priors to monocular 4D head reconstruction can hallucinate details that corrupt well-observed regions, while monocular overfitting causes geometric fragility and Gaussian drift that further degrade pseudo-ground truth generation.
AI.method: ConfAvatar introduces SDF-Opacity Co-Regularization (SOC) to anchor Gaussians to a coherent surface, computes view-dependent Gaussian confidence maps for novel views, and injects them at multiple scales into a pretrained diffusion prior to complete under-constrained regions without overwriting reliable content.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that ConfAvatar achieves state-of-the-art performance for monocular 4D head reconstruction, with code released on GitHub.
AI.conclusion: Coupling surface-anchored 3D Gaussians with confidence-guided diffusion completion resolves both identity corruption and geometric fragility in monocular 4D head reconstruction.

title: CHORES: Clutter-Robust Hand-Object Reconstruction with Geometry-Conditioned Target Disambiguation

AI.tldr: This paper proposes CHORES, an end-to-end monocular 3D Hand-Object Interaction (HOI) reconstruction architecture for cluttered environments, achieving state-of-the-art results on DexYCB, HO3D, and ObMan.
AI.motivation: Existing monocular 3D HOI reconstruction methods assume single-object scenes and suffer from severe target ambiguity in cluttered real-world environments with background distractors.
AI.method: CHORES integrates global metric depth priors for absolute scale constraints, uses a Physical-Aware Interaction Refinement (PAIR) module to identify the active target via hand-object geometric affordance, and applies geometry-guided anchor initialization for point queries.
AI.result: On DexYCB, HO3D, and ObMan, CHORES achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving F-score by 4.8% and reducing Chamfer Distance by 9.1% over the strongest baseline on DexYCB.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly modeling hand-object geometric affordance and metric depth priors enables accurate 3D HOI target disambiguation and reconstruction in cluttered multi-object scenes.

title: Recursive Entropic Variational Inference for Nonlinear State-Space Models

AI.tldr: This paper presents a class of recursive entropic variational inference algorithms for state estimation in nonlinear, non-Gaussian state-space models.
AI.motivation: State estimation in nonlinear, non-Gaussian state-space models requires tractable inference schemes that maintain dynamic consistency while handling general nonlinearities.
AI.method: The approach casts Bayesian inference as a sequence of entropic trust-region updates subject to dynamic consistency constraints via a variational Lagrangian formulation, deriving forward-backward recursive schemes under Gauss-Markov approximations and closing recursions with generalized statistical linear regression and Fourier-Hermite moment matching.
AI.result: The paper derives a family of recursive forward-backward state estimation algorithms with favorable computational complexity for general nonlinear, non-Gaussian models.
AI.conclusion: The variational Lagrangian entropic trust-region formulation provides a unified and computationally efficient framework for recursive Bayesian filtering and smoothing.

title: On $\ell_0$-Regularized Sparse Multiple Kernel Learning for Feature Selection

AI.tldr: This paper studies direct l0-regularized sparse multiple kernel learning (SMKL) via mixed-integer min-max optimization, selecting fewer kernels than l1-MKL with comparable test accuracy on synthetic and UCI datasets.
AI.motivation: Conventional l1-regularized MKL entangles sparsity induction with kernel-scale control, making it difficult to explicitly control the number of selected kernels or features.
AI.method: The authors formulate l0-MKL and an l0-lp MKL framework as min-max mixed-integer optimization problems (outer kernel selection, inner SVM) solved to within a prescribed tolerance of global optimality, and show that for feature-wise rank-one linear base kernels the l0 constraint bounds the combined kernel rank.
AI.result: Experiments on synthetic and UCI benchmark datasets show that l0-regularized SMKL selects fewer kernels than conventional l1-MKL while maintaining comparable test accuracy and generally outperforming an alternating best-response heuristic.
AI.conclusion: Explicit l0 regularization disentangles support selection from kernel weight scaling in SMKL, supporting feature selection and confirming that less sparse solutions can still perform better.

title: IRL-GAD: Graph Anomaly Detection via Inverse Reinforcement Learning as Normality Modeling

AI.tldr: This paper proposes IRL-GAD, a graph anomaly detection method that models normality via inverse reinforcement learning on hop-wise GAT attention policies and evaluates it across six static benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Representation-based graph anomaly detection methods treat anomalies as statistical outliers in a fitted representation, which can fail when anomalous nodes are camouflaged near benign nodes.
AI.method: IRL-GAD represents each node's hop-wise GAT attention distributions as soft aggregation policies in a Node-MDP surrogate, fits a normal-reference reward from benign nodes using maximum-entropy inverse reinforcement learning (MaxEnt-GIRL), and scores candidates by cumulative KL divergence from the induced reference policy.
AI.result: The method is evaluated across six static benchmarks spanning homophilic citation, camouflage-oriented fraud, organically labeled social-interaction, and large-scale citation graphs, with structural and semantic reward components reported as diagnostics.
AI.conclusion: Modeling deviations from learned benign aggregation mechanisms via inverse reinforcement learning offers a complementary aggregation-based perspective for detecting camouflaged graph anomalies.

title: Hyperparameter Optimization for Small-Sample Machine Learning via Design of Experiments

AI.tldr: This paper applies design of experiments (DOE) principles to hyperparameter optimization in small-sample regimes, reducing validation-to-test error bias by 73-99% across fourteen datasets while finding that no tested tuning method consistently beats untuned models.
AI.motivation: In small-sample datasets, standard hyperparameter tuning methods such as grid search and Bayesian optimization suffer from reduced generalization, poor validation-test correlation, and overly optimistic error estimates.
AI.method: The authors fit a response surface to a space-filling design over the hyperparameter space to select optimal hyperparameter sets.
AI.result: Across fourteen public datasets and Monte Carlo simulations, the DOE method achieves similar generalizable test error to grid search and Bayesian optimization while reducing validation-test error bias by 73-99%, and none of the evaluated tuning methods consistently outperform untuned models.
AI.conclusion: Space-filling design of experiments substantially reduces validation optimism in small-sample hyperparameter tuning, while raising questions about whether hyperparameter optimization consistently improves test error in small-data regimes.

title: Min-p, Max Exaggeration: A Critical Analysis of Min-p Sampling in Language Models

AI.tldr: This paper critically re-examines the ICLR 2025 Oral paper on min-p sampling and finds that its four main lines of evidence fail to support claims that min-p improves quality, diversity, or their trade-off over baseline samplers.
AI.motivation: Min-p sampling was claimed to outperform basic, top-k, and top-p sampling in quality and diversity, warranting a rigorous verification of the underlying empirical and methodological evidence.
AI.method: The authors reanalyze the original human evaluation data and statistical tests, conduct comprehensive hyperparameter-controlled sweeps on GSM8K CoT and GPQA, audit the LLM-as-a-Judge reporting, and verify the community adoption claims.
AI.result: Reanalysis shows min-p did not outperform baseline samplers in human evaluations, GSM8K CoT, or GPQA when controlling for hyperparameter count; LLM-as-a-Judge scores were inconsistently reported; and the 54k repository / 1.1M star adoption claims were unsubstantiated and removed from the camera-ready version.
AI.conclusion: The evidence presented in the original min-p paper does not support the claim that min-p improves generation quality, diversity, or their trade-off over established samplers.

title: PDAC: Efficient coreset selection for continual learning via probability density awareness

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Probability Density-Aware Coreset (PDAC) and its streaming variant SPDAC to efficiently construct replay memory buffers for rehearsal-based continual learning by prioritizing high-density samples.
AI.motivation: Mainstream coreset selection methods for rehearsal-based continual learning typically solve a bi-level optimization problem with many inner and outer iterations, which incurs substantial computational cost and limits practical efficiency.
AI.method: The authors analyze the Mean Squared Error between the buffer-trained model and the Bayes-optimal model via localized error decomposition, showing that high-probability-density samples dominate error suppression; they then use a Projected Gaussian Mixture (PGM) model to estimate joint sample density for density-prioritized buffer selection (PDAC) and introduce streaming Expectation Maximization to adapt PGM parameters to streaming data (SPDAC).
AI.result: Extensive comparative experiments across various continual learning settings show that PDAC and SPDAC outperform baseline methods while maintaining favorable computational efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Prioritizing high-probability-density samples via PGM density estimation provides an efficient and effective alternative to bi-level optimization for coreset selection in continual learning.

title: Silent Unpairing: How Mid-Training Probes Break Same-Seed Comparisons and Can Enable Selection Bias

AI.tldr: This paper diagnoses how arm-specific mid-training probes can desynchronize random streams or data cursors in same-seed deep-learning comparisons and enable nonnegative reporting optimism when selection is performed on the affected quantity.
AI.motivation: Same-seed comparisons are used to control run-to-run variation, especially in autonomous experimentation by AI agents, but mid-training probes that advance shared random streams or data cursors can silently break this control and put reproducibility at risk.
AI.method: The authors prove a sufficient condition for bitwise trajectory identity under state-pure probes, characterize the first update-level violation, separate reporting optimism from systematic placement effects with offset and scale decompositions, audit 28 codebases, and evaluate dynamic witnesses including Meta-Weight-Net and nanoGPT.
AI.result: Auditing 28 codebases finds 22 exposed, 4 guarded, and 2 configuration-dependent cases; on Meta-Weight-Net, localizing the first divergent consumer restores state identity with a probe-free baseline on 5/5 seeds; selecting on the reported quantity yields a 4.01-point uplift over the placement average in one single-rig campaign (though validation-to-test bridge intervals include zero), and a nanoGPT campaign predicts 0.003884 loss units before 16 held-out seeds yield 0.003431.
AI.conclusion: Autonomous experimentation pipelines can inadvertently trigger probe-induced desynchronization and selection optimism, which can be mitigated through probe-state isolation, deterministic execution, and repeat checks with explicit verification scopes.

title: Localized Operator Learning with Adaptive Partition-of-Unity Mixture-of-Expert Networks

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a partition-of-unity (POU) mixture-of-experts framework for localized neural operator learning, including HiRefPOU for DeepONets and a POU extension for Fourier Neural Operators (FNOs).
AI.motivation: Existing operator learning methods such as DeepONets and FNOs often struggle on PDE families that exhibit sharp interfaces, heterogeneous coefficients, and localized multiscale structures.
AI.method: Geometry-aware gating networks produce smooth spatial partitions that blend local expert networks; HiRefPOU organizes localized representations in DeepONets as a residual-style hierarchical POU architecture with nested parent-child partitions that preserve global continuity, while the same POU principle is added to FNOs for spatial adaptivity without altering spectral layers.
AI.result: On heterogeneous Darcy and reaction-diffusion benchmarks, HiRefPOU achieves substantially lower error than global DeepONet and static POU-MoE baselines, and learned partitions align with interfaces and regions of rapid solution variation, though localization benefits depend on PDE structure and backbone choice.
AI.conclusion: Explicit geometric localization through adaptive partition-of-unity mixture-of-experts improves both accuracy and interpretability in neural operator learning for multiscale and heterogeneous PDEs.

title: Spectral Condition for $\mu$P under Width–Depth Scaling

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a unified spectral framework for maximal update parameterization (muP) under joint width-depth scaling in deep residual networks, identifying a transition from k=1 to k>=2 transformations per block and validating CompleteP-style parameterization on GPT-2 style language models.
AI.motivation: Scaling generative foundation models in both width and depth challenges stable feature learning and hyperparameter (HP) transfer, and existing extensions of muP to joint width-depth scaling are fragmented, architecture- and optimizer-specific, and rely on technically involved theories.
AI.method: For deep residual networks with k transformations per residual block, the framework specifies how weight norms and per-step update norms scale with width and depth, and maps these spectral constraints to concrete, optimizer-specific HP parameterizations across a broad class of optimizers.
AI.result: The framework reveals a fundamental transition from k=1 to k>=2 that unifies prior muP formulations and identifies CompleteP-style parameterization (k>=2) as suited for multi-transformation architectures like Transformers; in GPT-2 style language model experiments, CompleteP-style parameterization achieves stable feature learning and robust HP transfer under width-depth scaling, whereas standard parameterization and Depth-muP-style parameterization (k=1) often fail.
AI.conclusion: The proposed spectral framework provides a simple, unified recipe for implementing muP across optimizers under joint width-depth scaling, with practical effectiveness supported by GPT-2 style language model experiments.
